stories.title: ‘Husband's death should look natural’, says snakebite murder accused:Wife searched venomous snakes on Google
stories.summary: In the first part of this story, we explained how Damini, accused of orchestrating her husband Atul's death through a snakebite in Meerut, became involved in an extramarital relationship. The second and final part details how her married boyfriend Tushar allegedly helped execute the plan with the assistance of snake charmers, in an attempt to make the killing appear to be a natural death. 'It should look like a natural death' According to the police investigation, Damini allegedly told Tushar one day- Kill Atul in such a way that it doesn't look like murder, but a natural death. You remember the Ravita-Amardeep case from April 2025. It happened in our neighbouring village, where Ravita and her lover left a snake on her husband's bed. Why don't we do the same? Tushar allegedly agreed with the idea and said he knew two snake charmers, Sonu and Uday, from Khadar Basti. He reportedly approached them, saying- Someone has to be killed through a snakebite, but it should not appear to be murder. It should look like a normal death. When the snake charmers asked who the target was, Tushar allegedly replied that it was the husband of a female friend who wanted to get rid of him because he was causing her distress. Police claim a deal was struck for ₹5 lakh, with an advance payment of ₹15,000. The snake charmers allegedly instructed Tushar that Atul would first need to be heavily intoxicated or rendered unconscious before they released the snake. They also said the snake would have to be kept hungry to increase the likelihood of it biting. The alleged plan was scheduled for the night of 17 July. Google search for the most venomous snake After finalising the arrangement, Tushar allegedly informed Damini that the plan would involve a venomous snake, ensuring that the post-mortem would indicate death by snakebite and arouse no suspicion. He allegedly warned her not to repeat the mistake made in the 2025 Ravita case, where investigators concluded the husband had actually been strangled before a non-venomous snake was placed on the bed. According to the investigation, Damini said she had already searched Google to learn- Tushar allegedly told her there was no need to search further and showed her a photograph on his mobile phone of the snake that would allegedly be used. Police claim it was a black krait, one of India's most venomous snakes, which had deliberately been kept hungry. Sleeping pills mixed into milk According to the police, on the night of 16 July, Damini and Atul had dinner together before Atul went to bed. Damini allegedly went into the kitchen, mixed sleeping tablets into a glass of milk and gave it to Atul before lying down beside him. At around 2 am, she allegedly got out of bed, picked up her seven-year-old son, Manik, and left the bedroom. She then lay down with him on a cot outside the room and allegedly called Tushar, telling him- Come now. Atul is asleep. Snake released inside the bedroom Police allege that Tushar then arrived at the house with snake charmers Sonu and Uday, carrying a box containing a live black krait. Damini allegedly led them into the bedroom. According to investigators, the snake charmers advised that the snake should be released directly onto the bed to prevent it escaping. Damini allegedly handed them a bedsheet. The four allegedly covered Atul with the sheet before Sonu and Uday lifted one side and released the hungry krait onto the bed. Police claim the snake bit Atul's feet two or three times. The three men allegedly waited for around 20 minutes, checked whether Atul had died and then left the house. Before leaving, Tushar allegedly instructed Damini to begin crying and raising the alarm the following morning before going back to sleep. Damini then allegedly slept beside her son. Morning drama to make the death look natural At around 6 am on 17 July, Damini allegedly entered the bedroom carrying tea for Atul. According to the police, she pretended to wake him before screaming for help when he did not respond. Neighbours gathered after hearing her cries. She allegedly told them Atul had been bitten by a snake and pointed to the snakebite marks on his foot, saying there was still a snake inside the room. Initially, neighbours believed Atul had died from a snakebite. However, members of Atul's family became suspicious. His elder brother informed the police. When officers arrived, they found Damini sitting beside her husband's body, crying. How police uncovered the alleged conspiracy During questioning, police asked Damini how Atul had died. She allegedly said she had left the bedroom during the night because it was too hot and had slept outside with her son. Investigators said they found her explanation suspicious. Police then examined her call records and allegedly discovered that she had spoken several times during the night to Tushar Payla. After Tushar was detained, investigators claim he disclosed the entire alleged conspiracy involving Damini and the two snake charmers.

stories.title: How to check if petrol contains only 20% ethanol:File a complaint if you suspect irregularities; can also be used for cooking, govt to provide subsidy
stories.summary: When filling petrol in a bike or car, many motorists wonder how much ethanol is blended with the fuel. Is it 20%, or more? While it cannot be identified by sight or smell, there is a simple test that can help estimate the ethanol content. Meanwhile, the Central Government is also preparing a major policy to promote ethanol as a domestic cooking fuel. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is working on a new policy under which ethanol will be promoted as an alternative to LPG for household cooking. How to check whether petrol contains E20 Ethanol ? Petrol and ethanol mix completely, making it impossible to distinguish them visually or by smell. However, you can carry out a simple water test in about two minutes. Since ethanol dissolves in water, the petrol separates out. The water-ethanol mixture settles at the bottom. According to the government and public-sector oil companies, claims that petrol contains more than 20% ethanol are false. They state that only E20-grade petrol is currently being supplied. How to check whether your vehicle is E20-Compatible ? You can verify whether your vehicle supports E20 fuel by- Most vehicles manufactured after April 2023 carry an E20 Compatible sticker. For vehicles manufactured before 2023, prolonged use of E20 fuel is claimed to potentially affect rubber hoses, gaskets and fuel injectors over time. Owners of older vehicles are advised to- Where to report suspected fuel adulteration If your water test indicates ethanol or water content above 20%, or if an E20 information board is not displayed at a petrol station, complaints can be lodged through the following channels- Government plans to introduce Ethanol for household cooking Ethanol is a highly flammable liquid and will not be stored in existing LPG cylinders. Instead, the proposed system will use specially designed ethanol-compatible cooking stoves and fuel containers, which are expected to meet safety standards. The government's objective is to expand the use of biofuel (ethanol) beyond transport and into household kitchens. Subsidy planned for Ethanol stoves and fuel The proposed policy includes financial support to encourage adoption. 'Ethanol ATMs' planned at fuel stations Under the proposed scheme, 'Ethanol ATMs' will be installed at petrol pumps and retail outlets. Consumers will be able to fill special ethanol canisters, take them home and use the fuel in ethanol-compatible cooking stoves. When will Ethanol cooking become available? The ethanol cooking initiative is still in the planning stage. The government's new policy is expected to be announced by September 2026, after which the required infrastructure will be developed. The system is therefore expected to become available to the public towards the end of 2026 or later. The government has clarified that ethanol is intended as an alternative to LPG, not a replacement. Consumers will be free to choose either LPG or ethanol, depending on their preference and convenience. It has also stated that reports claiming LPG cylinders will be discontinued from 1 October 2026 are false. Aim is to reduce LPG imports India imports a significant share of its LPG requirements. According to the government's estimates, if 7 billion litres of ethanol are used annually for domestic cooking, the country could save billions of rupees in foreign exchange by reducing LPG imports.

stories.title: Premanand Maharaj's new ashram draws attention after Virat-Anushka visit:Built on nearly 9 bigha land in Mathura, also equipped with dialysis unit
stories.summary: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma arrived at Saint Premanand Maharaj's new ashram Yamuna Vihar Kunj in Vrindavan on July 22 (Wednesday). Both stayed in the ashram for about 1 hour. When they came out, Virat had a sandalwood tilak on his forehead and prasad in his hand. This is the same ashram about which devotees have been wanting to know for the past two months. Saint Premanand Maharaj has left his old Keli Kunj ashram and is performing bhajan-sadhana here. He gives darshan to devotees here. Why did Maharaj leave Keli Kunj ashram and make a new abode on the banks of Yamuna? What is the way to reach here? To know the answers to these questions, Dainik Bhaskar's team reached the ashram. They gathered information by talking to people and observing the routes leading to the ashram and the arrangements there. Read the full report Premanand Maharaj Shifted from Keli Kunj to the Banks of Yamuna Saint Premanand Maharaj has been spending very little time in his old Keli Kunj ashram for the past 2 months. He has also postponed his foot pilgrimage since May 18. Poor health has been cited as the reason behind this. A few days ago, a video of Saint Premanand giving discourse to his disciples on the banks of Yamuna also surfaced. In this video, he asked everyone to chant the name of Radha and not to follow him. Meanwhile, news has emerged that Premanand Maharaj has shifted to his new ashram, Yamuna Vihar Kunj Ashram. He is also giving darshan to devotees from here. Now know about the ashram New ashram is 15 kilometers away from Keli Kunj Ashram Premanand Maharaj's trust, Shri Hit Radha Keli Kunj, has built a new ashram named Yamuna Vihar Kunj. It is built on the banks of the Yamuna near Jahangirpur village in Mant tehsil. It is about one kilometer away from the Lakshmiji temple located in Belvan. It is about 15 kilometers by road from Kali Kunj Ashram. To see the ashram, our team crossed the Yamuna by steamer from Keshighat. After that, we reached Belvan Temple through muddy and uneven roads. ‘Only administration and ashram people are allowed inside’ Near the Lakshmi Temple in Belvan, an unpaved road leads to the ashram. Gravel was being laid on this road. Meanwhile, volunteers were present, setting up camps nearby. We were moving towards the ashram when the volunteers stopped us with folded hands. They said, no one is allowed to enter the ashram without permission. Only those people are allowed to go further who have received permission from the chief volunteer. After the volunteers stopped us, we stood there. Just then, vehicles of the SDM of Mant, CO, and other officers arrived there. The volunteers did not stop these vehicles. These vehicles moved forward without any hindrance. When I asked the volunteers, they said that vehicles of the administration and the ashram are allowed to go inside. After this, we talked to the local people about the ashram. People, without appearing on camera, said that here volunteers allow people to come and go based on instructions received from the ashram. However, farmers of the village can use this path to go to and from their fields. There are two ways to reach the ashram First route- This route goes from Keli Kunj Ashram via Varah Ghat to the Khadar region beyond Saubhari Van. From here, cross the Yamuna by boat or steamer and walk about 2 kilometers to reach the ashram. Second Route- This is a road route. In this, you will reach Mathura Road from Keli Kunj Ashram. From here, one reaches Belvan Temple via Yamuna Expressway Link Road and then through Jahangirpur village. From here, the ashram is about one kilometer inside. It takes 30 to 45 minutes to reach by this route. Yamuna Vihar Kunj built on nearly 9 bighas of land In this conversation, we came to know that the land on which the ashram is being built belonged to Mangal Singh, a resident of Jahangirpur village. After that, we searched and reached Mangal Singh's house. Here we met Mangal's son, Moolchand. Moolchand says - About 5 acres (about 8.75 bigha) of land has been taken from our family for the ashram. Out of this, 2 bigha of land was taken 3 months ago. The remaining land was taken a month ago. Out of this, about one bigha of land has permanent construction. The rest has huts and trees planted. The ashram has been built very beautifully. 2 Halls, Dialysis unit and flood protection system Moolchand said - The ashram has 2 large halls, where Maharaj ji performs satsang and serves Radharani. A dialysis machine has been installed in a container here. Doctors perform Premanand Maharaj's dialysis from time to time. To prevent floodwaters from reaching the ashram, a platform about 7-8 feet high has been built along the Yamuna riverbank. After this, high boundaries have been constructed. When we tried to find out from Moolchand how much land was given for the ashram, he did not disclose anything. Later, we found out that the rate for the land where the ashram is built is approximately 55 lakh rupees per hectare. New abode chosen for peace and solitude Local residents said that Saint Premanand Maharaj chose Yamuna Vihar Kunj because the calm and natural environment along the Yamuna river is conducive to solitary devotion and meditation. Compared to Kali Kunj Ashram, there is less crowd here. This allows him time for spiritual practice and contemplation. This is why he is staying here these days, engaged in devotion and meditation. Not everyone is allowed to go to Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Servants are stationed at various points along the way, who stop people one kilometer before the ashram. Saint Premanand Maharaj will give darshan in both ashrams on Guru Purnima Saint Premanand Maharaj will celebrate the Guru Purnima festival in both his ashrams. Preparations are underway in both Keli Kunj and Yamuna Vihar Kunj ashrams. From July 23 to 28, Saint Premanand Maharaj will give darshan to devotees in Yamuna Vihar Kunj. After this, on July 29, he will meet devotees at Kelly Kunj Ashram. Kelly Kunj Ashram has been specially decorated for Guru Purnima. From the main gate to the ashram premises, placards with religious messages have been put up. Charan Pujan (worship of feet) will be performed every day during the Guru Purnima festival at Kelly Kunj Ashram.

stories.title: Three reel-enthusiast sisters marry their cameraman:Take seven vows at Amroha temple; Hindu groups call it violation of tradition
stories.summary: Three sisters in Amroha who make reels have claimed to marry their own cameraman. All three are between 18 and 20 years old. They worshipped at the Chamunda Mata Temple and took seven vows around the fire, considering it a witness. The cameraman applied vermilion to their foreheads and the brides touched their husband's feet to seek blessings. However, no one from either family attended the wedding. This marriage came to light when the video surfaced on Wednesday at 5 PM. Leaders of Hindu organizations say that marrying in such a way at a religious place is a violation of Sanatan Dharma. Decorum has been broken. Seeing the opposition, the three sisters released a video defending themselves. They said, "In ancient times, there was King Dasharatha, who had three queens. Was that an insult then?" The three girls got married on July 17. 3 pictures of the wedding- Know the full story Saroj (20 years old), Savitri (19 years old), and Santosh (18 years old), residents of Dhauria village, are real sisters. All three are social media influencers. They create video content on Instagram-Facebook. They have IDs on Facebook and Instagram, on which only 27 videos are currently uploaded. All three have a good fan following on social media. They have over 4.69 lakh followers on Instagram and more than 84 thousand on Facebook. Vikas alias Vikku, a resident of Shyampuri village, is the cameraman for the three sisters. He had been working for the three sisters for the past 6 months. He also played the role of husband in stories related to the village. Elder bride is pursuing B.Tech, groom is intermediate pass Saroj is a second-year B.Tech student, while Savitri and Santosh have passed 12th grade. Their father Ramesh is a farmer. Vikku passed 12th grade this year. He now wants to pursue LLB. He is the youngest of three brothers. After marriage, Vikku is living at his in-laws' house. Saroj, Savitri, and Santosh stated- They have been together since childhood and did not want to be separated in the future either. When their family members tried to arrange their marriages in different places, they decided to marry the same cameraman together, rather than being separated. According to Vikas, he was aware of their feelings and situation. Therefore, he married all three with the intention of keeping them together. Dr. Shivcharan Das, manager of Chamunda Mata Temple, said , At the time the marriage was being discussed, beautification work was going on in the temple. No priest was present there. Trader leader opposed the marriage Local people and Hindu organizations, including trader leader Mukesh Gupta, have strongly objected to this marriage. They say that such an act at a religious place is a violation of Sanatan Dharma and social norms. They have appealed to society to take strict action against such people. 'We are happy with the marriage' In response to people's protest, the three sisters released a video. They said - We have not done anything wrong. It's all about love. All three of us can be happy together. There is nothing wrong with it. When we are happy and we have gotten married, what's the problem with that? All three of us are adults. Hasanpur Kotwali in-charge Rajesh Kumar Tiwari said that the sisters who got married stated that they got married at Chamunda Temple of their own free will.

stories.title: UP's oldest Samajwadi Party MLA Alambadi Azmi dies:Took his last breath at 90; won Assembly elections from Azamgarh five times
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party's oldest MLA, Alambadi Azmi, has died at the age of 90 after a prolonged illness. He breathed his last late on Wednesday night at his residence in Azamgarh. A five-time MLA from the Nizamabad Assembly constituency, Azmi will be laid to rest at 4 pm on Thursday. On 13 April, he was admitted to Medanta Hospital in Lucknow after his health deteriorated. He continued to receive treatment there through May, June and July before being discharged a few days ago. Used a keypad mobile phone Born on 16 March 1936 in Azamgarh, Alambadi Azmi represented the Nizamabad Assembly constituency continuously from 1996 to 2007. Despite his long political career, he was known for his simple lifestyle. He continued to use a keypad mobile phone and wore clothes made from fabric costing ₹30 per metre, produced at the Tanda textile mill in Ambedkar Nagar. Azmi completed his Intermediate education at Islamia College, Gorakhpur, in 1953. He later earned a degree in Mechanical Engineering from Gorakhpur in 1956. Counted among Mulayam Singh Yadav's closest associates Known for his Gandhian values, Alambadi Azmi was regarded as one of Mulayam Singh Yadav's closest political associates and had a reputation as an exceptionally honest public representative. One incident often cited to illustrate his integrity dates back to the 1996 Assembly elections, when Mulayam Singh Yadav reportedly gave him ₹5 lakh to contest the election. Azmi returned the money to Mulayam Singh in Lucknow, saying he did not need it to fight the election. This gesture became one of the defining examples of his personal honesty and frugal lifestyle.

stories.title: Ghaghra river swells in UP, 28 flood posts on alert:Two killed by lightning in Sonbhadra; rain warning for 75 districts
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 69 districts of Uttar Pradesh, with heavy rainfall expected in 18 districts on Thursday. According to the IMD, the weather is likely to remain mainly clear in Bahraich, Shravasti, Balrampur, Siddharthnagar, Maharajganj and Kushinagar. In Lucknow, the sky has remained cloudy since Thursday morning. On Wednesday, several parts of the state recorded significant rainfall. Mau received the highest rainfall at 72 mm, followed by 70 mm in Lalitpur, 58 mm in Sonbhadra, and 41.5 mm in Prayagraj. Meanwhile, continuous rainfall over the past 10 days has caused rivers to swell across the state. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River is flowing above the danger mark, with floodwater entering riverside villages. Crocodiles have also been spotted on roads and in agricultural fields. In Sonbhadra, rising water levels in the Ghaghra River washed away the road leading to the district jail. In Varanasi, nearly 50 small and large temples between Assi Ghat and Namo Ghat have been submerged. Monsoon activity to remain weak until 25 July Regional Meteorological Centre scientist Atul Kumar Singh said the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal has weakened, while the monsoon trough has shifted south of its normal position. As a result, monsoon activity is expected to remain weak across Uttar Pradesh between 23 July and 25 July. The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at isolated places during this period but has not issued any heavy rain warning for the state. See 2 pictures from Wednesday- Why has the monsoon weakened? According to meteorologists, the decline in rainfall is primarily due to- These changes have shifted the focus of monsoon activity towards west-central India, reducing the likelihood of widespread rainfall across Uttar Pradesh. Weather likely to change again from 26 July The IMD expects the monsoon to become active again from 26-27 July. Following this, good rainfall is likely in many parts of Uttar Pradesh. If fresh weather systems develop, rainfall activity could intensify during the last week of July. IMD issues advisory for farmers and residents The Meteorological Department has advised farmers that heavy rainfall is unlikely over the next few days, and agricultural activities should be planned accordingly. Residents in areas where thunderstorms and lightning are expected have been urged to- Avoid standing in open areas. Stay away from trees during lightning. Keep clear of electricity poles and power lines. Why could UP receive less rain this monsoon? Dr M. Mohapatra, Director General of the India Meteorological Department, said La Niña-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are coming to an end, with weather patterns showing signs of shifting towards El Niño, which is generally associated with below-normal rainfall. He said this indicates that the 2026 southwest monsoon could be weaker than normal. In addition, reduced snow cover across the Northern Hemisphere between January and March this year may also affect the strength of the monsoon.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust to train priests from across India:No fee to be charged; trust to bear lodging and food expenses
stories.summary: A permanent school will be built in the Ram Mandir complex in Ayodhya for the training of priests. Priests will be trained according to Vedic and Ramanandi traditions for temples across the country. How will these priests be selected for training? How will applications be taken? This format is being prepared. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust decided in a meeting that this training will be completely free. The Trust will fully arrange for the accommodation and food of the 'Batuk' (young students/trainees). The Trust believes that when priests trained in Ayodhya serve in temples across the country and abroad, the religious tradition and worship methods here will gain a new identity. Devotees' trust will also increase. First 30 priests were trained, now a permanent school will be built Swami Govind Dev Giri, the treasurer of the Trust, says, ‘A one-year priest training program was conducted during the construction of the Ram Mandir. In this, about 30 priests were trained in worship methods, Vedic mantras, rituals, and religious procedures. Later, this program was stopped. Now the Trust has decided to make it permanent. It has not yet been decided in which part of the temple this school will be prepared. Work in this direction will be started soon with the consent of the Trust members’. What will be taught in the school? Here, not only chanting of mantras, but also the entire system related to temple management will be trained. After completing the training, priests will be able to serve in temples across the country. These will be the responsibilities of the committee The Trust has also formed a 9-member religious committee for the temple's religious arrangements. Among these, 5 members will be from Ayodhya's saint community and 4 from the Trust. Know the big decisions of the trust Official spokesperson to be appointed for the first time To provide accurate and regular information to people through the media, the Trust has decided to appoint an official spokesperson for the first time. Now, all official information and clarifications from the Trust will be issued through a single medium.

stories.title: SP set to finalise candidates for 46 UP Assembly seats:Purvanchal gets biggest share; 27 close-loss faces set for repeat
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) has almost finalised candidates for 46 Assembly constituencies ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The list includes 19 seats in Purvanchal, 13 in western Uttar Pradesh, and 14 in central Uttar Pradesh. According to party sources, the official list is expected to be released in September. SP is also likely to field the same candidates in 27 constituencies where the party lost by a margin of less than 5,000 votes in the 2022 Assembly elections. The party believes these seats can be won in 2027. However, finalising candidates remains a major challenge. While SP continues to follow its PDA (Pichda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak – Backward, Dalit and Minority) strategy, it is preparing to reduce the number of Muslim and Yadav candidates and give greater representation to leaders from other backward communities and Dalits. Party sources say Akhilesh Yadav is not relying solely on caste equations. He is also closely evaluating the booth-level performance and organisational work of every ticket aspirant. Dalit candidates likely on more than 20 general seats For the 2027 Assembly elections, SP is continuing with its PDA formula, while also ensuring that loyal upper-caste leaders within the party are not sidelined. According to party sources, the number of Muslim and Yadav candidates is expected to be reduced. In addition to the 84 Scheduled Caste (SC)-reserved constituencies, the party is planning to field Dalit candidates on 20–25 general seats. Akhilesh meets aspirants; recommendations won't count The party is seeking feedback from district units while finalising candidates. Akhilesh Yadav is personally holding meetings with district office-bearers and ticket aspirants. At the same time, he has made it clear that all party workers must accept the final decision on ticket distribution and that rebellion over nominations will not be tolerated. Akhilesh is also assessing what each aspirant has done to strengthen the party's vote base at the booth level. Their level of activity during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is also being evaluated. The SP chief wants candidates who can effectively manage booth-level challenges. Candidate selection is therefore being based on survey reports, local caste equations, public image and booth-level organisational work. Akhilesh has already made it clear that tickets will not be awarded based on recommendations. Only those who meet the party's selection criteria will be nominated. Candidate list to be released after Congress seat-sharing talks SP has consistently maintained that it intends to contest the Assembly elections in alliance with the Congress. However, the two parties are yet to reach an agreement on seat sharing. Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has sought 200 seats for the party, while SP is reportedly unwilling to offer more than 60 seats. Akhilesh Yadav has said that Congress must first explain its winning prospects on the constituencies it is seeking before any decision is taken. Once a seat-sharing agreement is reached, SP is expected to release its first list of Assembly candidates in September.

stories.title: Lucknow man impaled on four iron rods:14 KGMU doctors save him after complex surgery, transfusing seven units of blood and plasma
stories.summary: Doctors at King George’s Medical University (KGMU) Trauma Centre have given a new lease of life to a 23-year-old man after performing an extremely rare and complex surgery. The youth was impaled by four iron rods after falling from an under-construction building. The accident left him with severe injuries to several vital organs, including the lung, diaphragm, stomach, small intestine, spleen and urinary bladder. Doctors began emergency treatment as soon as he reached the trauma centre and saved his life after an eight-and-a-half-hour surgery. Accident occurred at construction site According to doctors, Umesh, a resident of Amritpur in Farrukhabad district, was working at an under-construction building in Lucknow’s Badshah Nagar on July 13 when he fell from a height onto iron reinforcement rods. Four rods pierced through his body, reaching his chest and abdomen. Local residents cut the protruding rods and rushed him to the KGMU Trauma Centre without removing them from his body. Patient Stabilized First When Umesh arrived at the trauma centre, he was suffering from heavy blood loss and his blood pressure was falling rapidly. Investigations revealed that one rod had pierced his left lung, while the others had severely damaged his small intestine, stomach, spleen, urinary bladder and diaphragm. As he had developed pneumothorax (air trapped around the lung), doctors first inserted a chest drain to stabilise his condition before proceeding with surgery. BP Suddenly Dropped During Surgery A trauma surgery team led by Prof. Dr Sameer Mishra and Dr Narendra Kumar began the operation. During the procedure, the patient’s blood pressure dropped sharply while one of the iron rods was being removed. Doctors from the trauma, anaesthesia and other specialist departments immediately managed the crisis and stabilised the patient. The team then carefully removed all four rods and successfully repaired three perforations in the urinary bladder, multiple injuries to the small intestine, as well as damage to the stomach, diaphragm and spleen. Condition is improving During the operation, the patient received three units of packed red blood cells (PRBC) and four units of fresh frozen plasma (FFP). Following the successful surgery, he was admitted to the ICU. Doctors said his blood pressure, pulse rate and oxygen levels have now returned to normal, and he is recovering steadily. As the patient comes from an economically weaker background, his treatment was provided free of cost with support from KGMU and the Chandrani Jain Charitable Trust. Team of 14 doctors performed 8.5-hour surgery Dr Sameer Mishra, who led the surgery, said the accident took place at around 4:30 am on Monday, and the patient reached the KGMU Trauma Centre before 6 am. After the initial assessment, he was shifted to the operation theatre at around 7:30 am. The complex surgery lasted for eight and a half hours, with a team of 20 people, including 14 doctors, involved in the treatment. The patient remained on ventilator support for two days after surgery before being shifted to the ICU ward. Dr Mishra said he could not attend the university’s convocation ceremony because he was performing the life-saving operation. The projects include road widening, strengthening and construction of new stretches. Road widening and strengthening works are being carried out to renovate key routes in the southern region, provide connectivity to the Gorakhpur–Varanasi four-lane highway and the Link Expressway, and improve travel between all major locations in line with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s vision. Along with four-lane connectivity on major roads, road widening and strengthening in rural areas are progressing at a war footing. The biggest beneficiary is the southern region, which remained backward for decades due to poor infrastructure. Once regarded as the district’s most underdeveloped area because of weak road connectivity, the region is now witnessing a complete turnaround. Improved road infrastructure is making travel to rural and key areas significantly easier. Earlier, pothole-ridden roads made access to healthcare, education and trade in the city a major challenge. Wide and strengthened roads have now changed the region’s landscape. District Magistrate Deepak Meena said Gorakhpur has achieved significant progress in road construction projects in line with the Chief Minister’s vision. He added that all ongoing projects have been directed to be completed within the stipulated timeframe while maintaining quality. As part of the expanding road network, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the Dhuriyapar–Uruwa–Shahpur–Belghat road widening project, worth more than ₹57 crore, on June 13. Over the next month through to March 2027, nine more road projects covering 118 km and costing over ₹445 crore are scheduled to be completed. Dimple says Wangchuk to end hunger strike on July 20:Reaches Jantar Mantar with MPs; says government does not care who lives or dies
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav reached Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Thursday and met social activist Sonam Wangchuk, who is sitting on a hunger strike. She met him around 3:30 pm. When Dimple reached the stage, slogans of “Inquilab Zindabad” were raised. She said the government does not care about who is living or dying. She claimed that Sonam Wangchuk told her that he would end his hunger strike on July 20. Dimple said, “I want to appeal to all the youth to join the march from here to Parliament on July 20. This is a fight for your rights and dignity.” During the visit, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke said, “Dimple Yadav requested Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike on July 20. She said that her party would take this fight forward in Parliament, but Sonam Wangchuk has not given any response on this yet.” Wangchuk has been demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue. He has been on an indefinite hunger strike for the past 19 days, during which his weight has dropped by 8.9 kg. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had also appealed to him on July 14 to end the protest. Dimple's 2 major points- ‘Fear is being created in the country’: Dimple Yadav said, “I salute Sonam Wangchuk’s hunger strike. The health of many students has deteriorated. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has provided a platform to the youth. If our youth become strong, no one can defeat them. The entire Samajwadi Party supports this. Everyone knows the condition of students and farmers in the country. An atmosphere of fear is being created.” ‘Government and BJP do not follow Gandhi’s ideals’: She said, “The government does not care who is living or dying. Such a harsh government has never existed in the country. BJP can be stopped in Uttar Pradesh through votes. They do not want to take responsibility. They do not follow Gandhi’s ideals. They only want to remain in power by using the name of Lord Ram.” 6 MPs and 1 MLA were present with Dimple Yadav Dimple Yadav was accompanied by six MPs and one MLA, including Samajwadi Party MPs Ruchi Veera from Moradabad, Dharmendra Yadav from Azamgarh, Narottam Patel from Fatehpur, Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur, Pappu Nishad from Sant Kabir Nagar, and SP MLA Ragini Sonkar from Machhlishahr. Priya Saroj had reached Jantar Mantar a day earlier Earlier on Wednesday (July 15), SP MP Priya Saroj had reached Jantar Mantar and said, “We stand with all the youth. Do not fear anyone and do not stop. We can move forward only through struggle. I will also raise your voice in Parliament.” Akhilesh called Wangchuk to inquire about his well-being SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had posted on X on Tuesday, July 14, in support of Sonam Wangchuk. He said he spoke to Wangchuk over the phone and enquired about his health while appealing to him to end the hunger strike. Akhilesh said the country needs Wangchuk’s moral leadership and that he should recover his health before starting a new movement. He also attacked the BJP, saying issues like the NEET paper leak and Ram Temple theft reflected the government’s failure. He further said global concern over Wangchuk’s protest was harming India’s democratic image under the BJP government. Nagina MP Chandrashekhar also reached Jantar Mantar Chandrashekhar also reached Jantar Mantar Bhim Army leader and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad also met Sonam Wangchuk at Jantar Mantar on July 15. He accused the government of dictatorship. Chandrashekhar said, “Sonam Wangchuk and many students have been on hunger strike for 10 days. It is painful for me too. I have limited time, otherwise I would have sat here with them.” He claimed that if he joined the protest even for a day, lakhs of people would gather there. He said the government should test people only to the extent that it is justified. CJP demands resignation of Education Minister The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has been staging a protest at Jantar Mantar since 20 June against the alleged NEET paper leak. The group is demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Activist Sonam Wangchuk has also joined the protest. CJP was formed after Chief Justice Surya Kant's remarks comparing unemployed youth to "cockroaches", a comment that sparked widespread criticism. The party alleged that the government has responded with silence to Wangchuk's efforts to raise issues affecting students. CJP founder Abhijeet Deepke said the government was avoiding accountability and described its approach as cruel. Wangchuk earlier spent 170 days in Jodhpur Jail Wangchuk had earlier spent 170 days in Jodhpur Central Jail while campaigning for full statehood for Ladakh. He was accused of inciting violence during a hunger strike in Leh on 24 September 2025, in which four people were killed and around 90 were injured. The government alleged that Wangchuk had provoked the violence. Two days later, on 26 September, he was detained under the National Security Act (NSA) and sent to Jodhpur Jail.

stories.title: Police leave Jauhar University after Azam's wife's intervention:'We have 15 days. Why are you sitting inside?'
stories.summary: Thirty-eight out of 40 buildings of Jauhar University, owned by former Uttar Pradesh minister and senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, have been declared illegal. The Rampur district administration has ordered demolition of these structures. After the order, Azam Khan’s wife Dr Tazeen Fatima reached Jauhar University on Thursday. She expressed anger after seeing police personnel deployed inside the university campus. She said, “We have a clear court order that gives us 15 days’ time. In such a situation, police and administration cannot forcibly sit inside the university like this. The entire action is being carried out with a sense of hostility.” Tazeen Fatima got the police personnel deployed on duty removed from the university premises. She then went to her office inside the campus, where she met the management and Samajwadi Party leaders. Discussions were held on the strategy to be adopted against the action by the Rampur Development Authority (RDA). Advice was also sought on challenging the District Magistrate’s order in court. SP leaders allege administration acted illegally After the meeting, city president Aseem Raja alleged that the order had given the university 15 days’ time, but it was not followed. “Forget 15 days, not even 15 minutes were given. Immediately after the order, police were deployed inside the university campus and a camp was set up. This is completely illegal,” he said. Administration gave decision within 10 minutes, claims SP leader SP leader Aseem Raja said the university management had submitted its reply to the notice issued on July 15 within the given time. “After this, the district administration called us to present our side verbally, and we appeared there. But the entire action was already decided. Our views were heard, but the decision was announced within just 10 minutes. A press release was issued immediately after that. This shows that the decision was pre-planned,” he said. He alleged that the action was being taken as part of a conspiracy to fulfil the wishes of certain officials and defame the university during the admission process. ‘Why harass us when 15 days were given?’ Aseem Raja said the order clearly provided the university 15 days to present its side, but the administration did not wait even for 15 minutes. “Immediately after issuing the order, police were deployed inside the campus and a counselling camp was set up. This is completely illegal and should be removed immediately,” he said. He added that the university had the right and time to approach the High Court. “The administration should respect the court and the time limit mentioned in its own order,” he said. Claim that all university buildings are legal Aseem Raja claimed that all buildings of Jauhar University are legal and approved maps are available. “If the district administration does not accept these documents, they will be presented before the High Court. The District Magistrate’s decision is not final. We will strongly present our case in court,” he said. He also said that the matter related to the university’s main gate is already pending before the court and a stay order is in place. “In such a situation, taking any action regarding the gate or the public road connected to it is not appropriate,” he added. Administration declares 38 buildings illegal District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi had rejected the objections raised by the university management on Wednesday (July 15). Following this, the Rampur Development Authority started the process of action. According to the RDA investigation, only two out of the 40 buildings inside the university campus had approved maps. stories.title: Sub-inspector refuses to return bribe money despite DIG's orders:Gonda SHO reprimanded; 'Your officer is bringing disrepute to the force'
stories.summary: “Your station's inspector took ₹30,000 in the name of filing a chargesheet. Later, he filed a final report in the case. What are you doing there? It's the SHO's job to ensure there's no corruption in the station. Now get his money returned, otherwise I'll suspend you. These people have increased corruption. They are all tarnishing the department's name. They have brought shame to the entire zone and the entire district.” These words were spoken by Devipatan Range DIG Ashok Kumar Shukla to the Tarbganj SHO over the phone in Gonda. The matter came up when the DIG was conducting a public hearing. Just then, a person arrived. He said that Inspector Om Prakash Yadav had taken ₹30,000 to file a chargesheet, but later filed a final report instead. After hearing the complaint, the DIG called the SHO and reprimanded him. He asked for the money to be returned immediately. The incident is from 9 July, but its video surfaced today. However, the victim claims that despite the DIG's reprimand, the money has not been returned yet. Read the entire case in detail King Upadhyay, a resident of Mannipura village in Tarbganj police station area, reached the DIG office on 9 July. There, DIG Ashok Kumar Shukla was listening to people's problems. King complained that Inspector Om Prakash Yadav, posted at Tarbganj police station, had taken ₹30,000 from him to file a chargesheet in an assault case, but later filed a final report. He said, "I have been telling the inspector for a month that if you haven't done my work, then return my money but he is neither answering calls nor replying to my messages." He also showed the DIG screenshots of messages sent to the inspector. Seeing this, the DIG became furious. Upon hearing the complaint, DIG Ashok Kumar Shukla immediately called the Tarbganj SO. He said, “SO Tarbganj, you have an inspector there named Om Prakash Yadav. I am sending you a photo of this case number. The inspector had taken ₹30,000 to file a chargesheet, but instead filed a final report on it.” “If there is basis for a chargesheet, then file the chargesheet. Get his ₹30,000 returned immediately, otherwise I will get it returned. You will do the work of sending him to jail. When the inspector took ₹30,000 from the person, what were you doing there? I have seen his WhatsApp chat,” the DIG said. “They are messaging the inspector to return my money. If he had the courage, he would have asked which money, what money are you talking about. He is sitting quietly because he must have taken the money. If there is such corruption, you will be suspended,” he said. My vehicle was vandalised Victim King Upadhyay said, “On January 23, 2026, Raja from the same village vandalised my car and broke the glass. When I protested, he assaulted me. I filed a case and pleaded with Inspector Om Prakash Yadav to file a chargesheet.” “The inspector demanded ₹30,000 from me for this. I gave the money in February. Later, the inspector filed the final report. We messaged him on WhatsApp to return the money. He said he had come on duty to Bahraich and would return it. stories.title: Maulana claims Lord Krishna offered namaz five times:Protests erupt in Lucknow; Ayodhya saint announces ₹10 lakh reward for cutting his tongue
stories.summary: A cleric from Etawah, Uttar Pradesh, Maulana Jarjis Ansari, has sparked a controversy with his remarks on Lord Krishna. The cleric claimed that Lord Krishna was a Muslim and used to offer namaz five times a day. He further said that if Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, whom he described as a devotee of Lord Ram, reads Islamic scriptures, he would start loving Islam. After a video of the Maulana’s remarks surfaced on social media on Thursday, Hindu organisations expressed strong objection. In Lucknow, the Hindu Mahasabha held a protest by trampling on pictures of Maulana Jarjis Ansari and submitted a complaint seeking an FIR at Hazratganj police station. Ayodhya saint Vishnu Das condemned the statement and announced a cash reward of ₹10 lakh for anyone who cuts off Maulana Jarjis Ansari’s tongue. The statement is reportedly from June 23, when Maulana Jarjis Ansari delivered a speech at a religious gathering held at Lakrbandha ground in Deoghar district of Jharkhand. Now know the complete matter in detail What did Maulana Jarjis Ansari say? Maulana Jarjis Ansari said, “If our brothers do not mind, even Krishna Ji used to offer namaz five times a day. If you do not believe it, look at the 10th verse of the sixth chapter of the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita.” He quoted the Sanskrit verse: “Yogi yunjit satatam aatmanam rahasi sthitah Ekaki yatachittatma niraashir aparigrahah.” The Maulana claimed that in this verse Lord Krishna was telling Arjuna that while worshipping God, a person should involve his entire body in yoga. He said, “Yogi does not mean the Yogi from Uttar Pradesh. ‘Yogi yunjit satatam aatmanam’ means one should connect the entire body. Worship should not be done only by standing and raising hands. The entire body should be involved.” He further claimed that if Hindus and Muslims read their own scriptures, they would start loving Islam. He said, “Yogi Ji is a great devotee of Ram. If he reads his own books, then believe me, he will start loving Islam because Islam is not only the religion of Muslims, it is also their religion. This same faith was presented by Ramchandra Ji and Krishna Ji as well.” by Ramchandra ji also, by Krishna ji also. This is not just for Muslims.' Experts say Maulana misinterpreted Gita verse Maulana Jarjis Ansari’s interpretation of the Bhagavad Gita verse has been questioned. The verse does not mention namaz or Islam anywhere. The verse is from Chapter 6, Verse 10 of the Bhagavad Gita. Its actual meaning is that a yogi should continuously focus his mind, body and soul on the Supreme God. A person should meditate in solitude, control the mind and senses, and free himself from desires and attachments. Hindu Mahasabha protests in Lucknow Members of the Hindu Mahasabha, led by spokesperson Shishir Chaturvedi, protested against Maulana Jarjis Ansari in Lucknow. They reached Hazratganj police station and submitted a complaint against him. Shishir said, “Maulana Jarjis called Lord Krishna a strict Muslim who offered namaz five times a day. This is a grave insult to Sanatan Dharma. We have come to get an FIR registered.” He added that if action was not taken, they would march towards the Chief Minister’s residence and later towards Akhilesh Yadav’s residence. He said, “Akhilesh Yadav spoke a lot about the Ram Temple donation theft case. At least say a few words for your ancestor Lord Krishna and register an FIR. You are from Etawah and Maulana Jarjis is also from Etawah.” Political reactions over the statement VHP says action should be taken Vishwa Hindu Parishad national spokesperson Vinod Bansal said such statements were not new. He said, “Earlier too, statements were made about Lord Shiva by Arshad Madani. People like Maulana Jarjis have crossed limits several times, but they do not feel ashamed. If someone speaks about them, groups immediately react, but making such comments about our deities is unacceptable. Action should be taken.” Congress calls it an attempt to create tension before elections Congress spokesperson Surendra Rajput said people should not pay attention to such statements. He said, “As elections approach, BJP supporters, whether they are extreme religious figures or such hardline clerics, will try to poison the atmosphere by making such statements. Strict action should be taken against such people.” Ayodhya saint says Maulana made remarks for publicity Ayodhya saint Dharmdas Maharaj said the Maulana made such remarks only to gain attention. He said, “The Maulana does not have knowledge and said too much in an attempt to get publicity. These events belong to thousands of years ago. Their history is only 1,300-1,400 years old. Before that, there was only Sanatan Dharma.” Ayodhya saint announces ₹10 lakh reward Ayodhya saint Vishnu Das said, “A Maulana has claimed that Lord Krishna was Muslim and offered namaz. Whoever cuts his tongue will be given a reward of ₹10 lakh.” He alleged that the statement hurt the sentiments of crores of Krishna devotees. He said, “He does not know even a single word of Sanskrit and is wrongly interpreting verses of the Bhagavad Gita. A case of sedition should be registered against him.” He also questioned Akhilesh Yadav, saying, “He calls himself a Yadav, but has not spoken a single word against this statement. Why does he remain silent against such Maulanas?”

stories.title: Two SP councillors face off in Gorakhpur:One withdraws nomination, six elected unopposed to new Municipal Corporation executive
stories.summary: In the Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation Board meeting, the names of six new executive members have been announced. As many as seven councillors had filed nominations for this. Among them, two SP councillors – Chandrabhan Prajapati from Ward No. 23 and Noor Mohammad from Ward No. 74 -- were contesting against each other. However, later, after persuasion by senior party leaders, Noor Mohammad withdrew his nomination. The remaining six people were elected unopposed. This election process took place on Thursday afternoon around 2:30 PM. These councillors were selected The executive members who have been selected include Anand Sahni (BJP) from Ward No. 54, Aarti Singh (BJP) from Ward No. 66, Rajesh Kumar (BJP) from Ward No. 22, Rajendra Tiwari (BJP) from Ward No. 36, Ritesh Singh (BJP) from Ward No. 17, and Councillor Chandrabhan Prajapati (SP) from Ward 23 Shaheed Shiv Singh Kshetri Nagar. After the formation of the Municipal Corporation's executive committee, the Deputy Chairman will be elected from among the members included in it. Six members of the old executive will be out Due to completion of tenure, six members of the current executive will leave their posts. These include BJP's Vice President Pawan Tripathi, Rishi Mohan Verma, Chhote Lal Yadav, Shravan Patel and Saroj Paswan. Apart from this, the tenure of Samajwadi Party councillor Ramesh Yadav is also ending. With the end of Vice President Pawan Tripathi's tenure, the election of a new Vice President will also be held from among the new members of the executive. All eyes are on this meeting of the Municipal Corporation, with the formation of the new executive, a new team will emerge that will determine the direction of important decisions and development works of the Municipal Corporation.

stories.title: VIDEO | Doctor dies by suicide after being slapped:Body recovered from Yamuna, parents inconsolable, hospital operator arrested
stories.summary: The body of the doctor who jumped into the Yamuna River in Auraiya was recovered on Thursday morning at 11 am after 18 hours. The SDRF team conducted a search operation and retrieved the body from the river. Upon seeing the body, the parents and wife broke down in tears. The father sat down on the riverbank, unconscious from crying. Before jumping into the river, the doctor had posted a video on Instagram accusing the brother-in-law of a hospital operator of slapping and assaulting him. The incident is from the city Kotwali area. The doctor had jumped into the river from the Yamuna bridge on Wednesday evening around 5 pm. In this case, the police have arrested the hospital operator. See pictures... Know the complete case Lakhimpur Kheri resident Dr. Saurabh Vajpayee was a BMS doctor. He practised at Ram Autar Hospital located in Tilak Nagar of Auraiya city. His family includes father Nandkishore, mother Shikha, brother Sharad, wife Ruby and a five-year-old son Hridyansh. On Wednesday evening around 5 pm, Saurabh reached Yamuna bridge. There he posted two videos on Instagram and then jumped into the river. In the first video, he alleged that Sarvesh Singh, brother-in-law of the owner of Ram Autar Hospital, slapped him. In the second video, he appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for justice. Read what the doctor said in the video? Dr. Saurabh said, "I work at Ramautar Hospital. Dr. SP Singh's brother-in-law Sarvesh Singh raised his hand on me. I had been asking to change my room for three months. When I didn't get a room, I started shifting my belongings myself. During this, he abused me, slapped me and choked my neck." He said that he reached Auraiya Kotwali, but an attempt was made to settle the matter there. His allegation was, "The SHO was also engaged in mediating a settlement." He said, "If I commit suicide, then Sarvesh Singh, his son and Gaurav Singh will be responsible for it. I still consider SP Singh as my elder brother, but these people will be responsible for my death." Body found on Thursday morning Till late Wednesday evening, police and divers conducted a search operation in the Yamuna river, but the doctor could not be traced. On Thursday morning, SDRF started the operation again. After about two hours, the doctor's body was recovered approximately 200 meters away from the spot where he had jumped. Mother Shikha Vajpayee kept saying while crying- My son is gone... my child is gone! Alas, we want action to be taken against Gaurav Singh... Seeing her husband's body, wife Ruby Vajpayee alleged, "My husband was killed by Sarvesh, SP Singh, Gaurav and 20-25 people together. After the incident, he had told me that these people were settling an old grudge because he had called the accused 'driver' instead of 'brother-in-law'. The police are also hand-in-glove with the accused." FIR on complaint of family members After the body was found, the police sent it for post-mortem. SP Abhishek Bharti said that a case has been registered against hospital operator SP Singh and his relative on the complaint of the family members. Hospital operator SP Singh has been arrested. ASP Alok Mishra said that both parties had come to the police station. It has come to light that the hospital operator's brother-in-law slapped him. An attempt was made to reach a settlement between both parties. Further action will be taken based on the investigation of the case.

stories.title: Students gherao BHU Vice-Chancellor's office:Proctorial Board intervenes as protesters question delay in Medical Superintendent taking charge
stories.summary: Students gheraoed the Vice Chancellor's office at Kashi Hindu University, on Thursday afternoon at 3 PM, demanding immediate charge handover to the newly appointed Medical Superintendent of Sir Sunderlal Hospital and Trauma Center In-charge. During this, male and female students raised slogans against the university administration, submitted a memorandum to the Vice Chancellor, and demanded a quick decision. The protest was led by student leaders Shivansh Singh and Harsh Tripathi. The students stated that despite new appointments being made to the concerned posts, the officers have not been formally handed over charge. This is affecting the hospital's administrative system and creating a state of confusion among employees and common people. Students gave a letter to the VC Student leader Shivansh Singh said that Sir Sunderlal Hospital is one of the most important medical institutions in the state. Not handing over charge to officers even after appointment in such an institution reflects serious administrative negligence. He said that if the transfer of responsibilities does not happen on time, unnecessary obstacles may arise in administrative and financial work. He demanded from the university administration that new appointments be given charge with immediate effect so that the hospital's operations can be conducted with complete transparency and accountability. He warned that if the university administration does not take any concrete decision in this matter within two days, students will be compelled to make the movement more widespread and intense. He said that the students' objective is not any kind of confrontation, but to ensure smooth and transparent administration in the university. Names not being announced after appointments Student leader Harsh Tripathi said that the continuation of work by old in-charges even after new appointments raises many questions. He said that the university administration should complete the charge handover process without any delay, so that the proper transfer of administrative powers, records and financial responsibilities can be ensured. According to him, transparent administration strengthens the credibility of the university.

stories.title: VIDEO | Cyclist killed after being run over by truck:CCTV shows him losing balance; another man has a narrow escape
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man died after being crushed under the wheel of a truck fitted with a concrete mixer machine, in Varanasi on Thursday morning. The accident was so horrific that the victim's intestines came out. While the truck was passing, the cyclist suddenly lost balance. He came under the rear wheel of the truck along with the bicycle. However, the second person sitting on the back of the bicycle narrowly escaped the truck. This incident occurred on the Azamgarh Highway in the Cholapur police station area. CCTV footage of the accident has also emerged. The police have seized the footage and started searching for the truck and its driver. See 2 pictures... Know the complete matter Nakhru Rajbhar alias Kallu (45), a resident of Jairampur Saraiya village, had come to his in-laws' village Pahadpur on Wednesday. On Thursday morning, he was going to Danaganj market on a bicycle with his relative for some work. Nakhru was riding the bicycle and his relative was sitting on the carrier. When they reached the highway, suddenly a truck with a concrete mixer passed by them. At that moment, for some reason, the balance of their bicycle got disturbed. Before he could control it, Nakhru along with the bicycle came between the two wheels of the truck. Before anyone could understand anything, the rear wheel of the truck ran over him. After the accident, people from nearby gathered. The police were informed. The police who reached the spot took possession of the body and sent it for post-mortem. Meanwhile, after the accident, the truck driver fled from the spot. Used to support family by running a cart Nakhru Rajbhar used to support his family by running a cart. His family includes wife Pummi Devi, three sons and one daughter. All four children study in the village school. As soon as the news of the accident was received, there was chaos in the family. Police says search is on for the driver and the truck Station in-charge Sadhuwan Ram Gautam said: An elderly person has died in a road accident. stories.title: Seven-year-old killed by school bus in Mathura:Grieving father holds child's body as protesters vandalise school, clash with police
stories.summary: A seven-year-old child died after being crushed under the wheel of a school bus in Mathura, on Thursday morning. After reaching school, the child was getting down from the bus when the driver moved the vehicle forward. The child fell and came under the wheel. He died on the spot. Upon receiving the information, the family members reached the accident site. The father started weeping, holding his son's body in his lap. Seeing the blood-soaked body of the child, the anger of the family members and villagers erupted. The enraged people vandalised the school premises and created a huge ruckus. After this, they took the child's body to Govardhan Road and blocked the road. The protesters insisted on the arrest of the accused driver. The police who arrived at the scene tried to pacify them, but they did not agree. After this, when the police tried to remove them, there was a scuffle between the villagers and the police. Currently, the family members are sitting on the road and the police are trying to calm them down. A large number of police personnel are deployed at the scene. The incident occurred in the Jainth police station area. See pictures Know the full story Nitin, the 7-year-old son of Gangdev, a resident of Pelkhu village, studied in Class-2 at Tilak Singh Inter College in Ral village. As usual, he reached school by bus around 8:30 AM on Thursday morning. According to eyewitnesses, the bus driver was intoxicated. When the bus reached the school campus, children started getting off. Nitin was still getting off when the driver moved the bus forward. The innocent child stumbled, fell down, and came under the bus's rear wheel. People nearby and children screamed, but by then, he was severely crushed by the wheel. The child died on the spot after being run over by the bus wheel. Family members vandalised the school Upon receiving information about the incident, family members and villagers reached the school. Seeing the child's body, people's anger erupted. The father, holding his blood-soaked son's body in his lap, started weeping. Meanwhile, angry people started creating a ruckus. People started looking for the driver. But he had fled from the scene. When the driver was not found, angry people vandalised the main gate of the school and the glass panes inside. The commotion continued in the school premises for a long time. Body placed on Govardhan Road, blocking it After this, the family members took Nitin's body to Govardhan Road. They placed the body and blocked the road. Upon receiving information about the jam, the police arrived. Officials tried to persuade the family members to clear the jam, but they remained firm on their demands. After this, the police tried to remove them. During this, there was some pushing and shoving between some villagers and policemen. The police tried to forcibly remove the people, but seeing the anger of the people, the police had to retreat. Currently, the family members are sitting on the road. They say that they will not move from there until action is taken against the accused driver. The police are continuously trying to persuade them.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya wins bronze in shooting championship:Strongman-politician has arsenal of over 200 firearms
stories.summary: Strongman MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, alias Raja Bhaiya, has won the bronze medal in the 49th UP State Shooting Championship. He scored 25 points in S-25 Clay Pigeon Trap Shooting (NR). The championship was held from 21 June to 30 June at Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range in New Delhi. Raja Bhaiya participated as competitor number 71. Results were declared on Wednesday. A video of his shooting has surfaced. In it, Raja Bhaiya can be seen taking aim. Raja Bhaiya is fond of weapons. Last year, on the occasion of Dussehra, he showcased his collection of more than 200 weapons. Raja Bhaiya is a seven-time MLA from Kunda constituency in Pratapgarh. He has formed his own party, Jansatta Dal, of which he is the national president. Raja Bhaiya is a lifetime member of the rifle association Raja Bhaiya is a lifetime member of the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI). He had mentioned in an interview that his father, Uday Pratap Singh, was also a shooter. Every year on the occasion of Dussehra, Raja Bhaiya worships the weapons kept in his arsenal. Last year, a video of his weapon worship on Dussehra also surfaced. In it, more than 200 domestic and foreign weapons were seen adorned on the table. These included pistols, revolvers, 12 bore guns, rifles and thirty carbines. During the weapon worship, Raja Bhaiya had said, “All these weapons are ours. What is ours, belongs to the supporters, and what belongs to the supporters, is ours.” Divorce case ongoing with wife Bhanvi Singh Raja Bhaiya's divorce case with his wife Bhanvi is ongoing. Bhanvi has been living separately from her husband in Delhi for several years. In November 2022, she filed a divorce petition in Delhi's Saket Court. Bhanvi had accused Raja Bhaiya of assault and illicit relations. On June 3, 2025, wife Bhanvi wrote a letter to the PMO alleging that Raja Bhaiya possesses a cache of illegal foreign weapons. Following this, on September 18, 2025, Bhanvi released a video of the weapons on social media. She claimed that there are some weapons in it that could cause mass destruction.

stories.title: Ramgarh Tal to get passenger boat service:GDA to spend ₹3 crore, fare set at ₹40 to ₹50
stories.summary: Work is underway to enhance facilities at Ramgarh Tal in Gorakhpur. After constructing floating cum pillar jetties around the lake, there is now consensus on operating passenger boats. Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA) has received permission from the Transport Ministry to purchase boats and operate them. The authority is planning to make this purchase. Approximately ₹3 crore will be spent on this. There is a plan to select an experienced firm for operation. The fare is estimated to be around ₹40 to ₹50. Through this boat, people can tour various areas of Ramgarh Tal. The floating jetties will serve as its platforms. If someone from RKBK wants to come to Naya Savera, they can park their vehicle in the parking there and come here by boat. After visiting, they can return by the same boat. Know the features of the boat- GDA is also going to build a floating jetty GDA Vice President said - Tourists will have facilities GDA Vice President Abhinav Gopal said, “There is a plan to purchase passenger boats for the convenience of tourists. It will be operated in Ramgarh Tal. Sitting on this, people will be able to go from one end of the lake to the other end. For this, some floating cum pillar jetties will also be built. A nominal fare will have to be paid for travelling on this.”

stories.title: Constable dies by suicide after leave is denied:Claims in final audio he is ending his life because of three police personnel
stories.summary: A 25-year-old police constable died by suicide with his service rifle at around 3 am on Thursday in Bulandshahr. A fellow constable tried to stop him, but the disturbed man fired a shot into the air. The colleague then ran to inform the outpost in charge. Before anyone could intervene, the constable shot himself. Police reached the spot and found him dead. City SP Abhishek Pratap identified the constable as Sudhir. Before his death, Sudhir recorded an audio message alleging that his station house officer (SHO) and two station clerks (munshis) were responsible for his death. He claimed that after complaining of stomach pain, the SHO had harassed him and sent him to the police lines. He also alleged that the two munshis ignored his requests. Sudhir's sister-in-law also alleged that he took his own life after being denied leave. Earlier, however, a fellow constable had said Sudhir had been under emotional stress because the woman he loved had married someone else a month ago. According to the colleague, Sudhir repeatedly said, "I want to die." Following the incident, SP Dinesh Kumar Singh attached SHO Rahul Chaudhary and the two munshis, Ankit and Sudhir, to the police lines pending an inquiry. A departmental investigation has been ordered against all three. The incident took place in the Lakhawati police outpost area of Aurangabad. Sudhir Thakur was a resident of Sangecha village in Iradatnagar, Agra. He had joined the police force only three months ago. After receiving news of his death, his father Jagveer reached the mortuary and broke down on seeing his son's body. Circle Officer Prakhar Pandey tried to console him. Colleague: 'He kept saying he no longer wanted to live' Sudhir was the second of three brothers. His elder brother Krishna (32) is a farmer, while his younger brother Pawan (21) is a student. His parents, Jagveer and Guddi Devi, support the family through farming. According to fellow constable Saurabh, Sudhir appeared restless despite sitting with colleagues late on Wednesday night. He repeatedly said he no longer wanted to live. At around 3 am on Thursday, Sudhir picked up his service rifle and began walking towards a canal a short distance from the Lakhawati outpost. Saurabh said he became suspicious and followed him. Sudhir asked him not to come any closer, but Saurabh refused. The two argued, during which Sudhir said he intended to end his life. When Saurabh tried to stop him, Sudhir fired a shot into the air. Saurabh then ran to alert the outpost in charge. Moments later, Sudhir placed the rifle against his neck and fired, collapsing onto the road. What Sudhir said in his audio message In the recording, Sudhir said that on 13 July, he developed severe stomach pain and informed munshis Ankit and Sudhir, but they ignored him. He said he later approached SHO Rahul Chaudhary, who became angry, mistreated him, verbally abused him and had him attached to the police lines. He said he had become so distressed by the treatment that he was resigning from both his job and his life. He alleged that the SHO and the two munshis were responsible for his suicide and ended the message by saying that he only wanted justice. Sister-in-law: 'He was harassed after asking for leave' Sudhir's sister-in-law Chinki said he had called his elder brother to say he was suffering from stomach pain. His brother advised him to apply for leave, but Sudhir said his request had been refused and that he had instead been harassed. She said the family received a call from a police officer at around 5 am informing them that Sudhir had died by suicide, after which they left for Bulandshahr. Sudhir had visited home about 15–20 days ago and had previously returned to appear for the Sub-Inspector recruitment examination.

stories.title: Rain lashes 10 UP cities, alert for 36 districts:Dashashwamedh Ghat steps submerged; Ghaghara swells in Ballia as residents demolish homes
stories.summary: Monsoon has regained momentum across Uttar Pradesh, with showers reported since Thursday morning in 10 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki and Jaunpur. Several roads in Lucknow have been waterlogged following the downpour. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for seven districts, including Lucknow. According to the department, heavy rain is likely over the next three hours in Amethi, Barabanki, Hardoi, Lucknow, Rae Bareli, Sitapur and Unnao. Winds of 40–50 kmph and lightning are also expected during this period. Cloud cover persists over most parts of the state, and the IMD has issued a rain alert for 36 districts today. Rising water levels in rivers, fuelled by rainfall in the hills, have begun affecting parts of Uttar Pradesh. In Ballia, erosion has started along the banks of the Saryu and Ghaghara rivers. In Bansdih, residents are demolishing their permanent homes and relocating, with around 150 families having left so far. In Varanasi, rising water levels in the Ganga have submerged the first three steps of Dashashwamedh Ghat. However, the river is still 11.90 metres below the danger mark. In Mathura, the Yamuna is in spate, flowing 1.30 metres below the warning level, while the steps of Keshi Ghat in Vrindavan have gone underwater. In Prayagraj, the Ganga and Yamuna have reached the row of shops along the ghats. On Tuesday, rain was recorded in 40 cities across the state. Despite the recent showers, Uttar Pradesh has received 25 per cent less rainfall than normal since 1 June. Rain-bearing clouds disappear from 80% of the state According to the IMD, dry winds blowing in from Pakistan have pushed rain-bearing clouds away from nearly 80 per cent of Uttar Pradesh. As a result, more than half the state has seen little or no rainfall.

stories.title: Eight fire tenders tackle massive Lucknow fire:Dairy, furniture, grocery, welding and AC repair shops destroyed
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in shops built along the roadside on IIM Road, in Muktakipur, Madiyanv area of Lucknow, early on Thursday morning. The fire engulfed several shops within a short time. Upon receiving information at 1 AM, fire department teams reached the spot. With the help of about eight fire tenders, the fire was completely brought under control after about two and a half hours of effort. Shops, including New Bharat Milk Dairy, a furniture shop, a tea shop, Nadeem General Store, a welding shop, a grocery store, an AC repair shop, and others, were gutted in the fire. Two fire tenders arrived, later six more were called According to the fire department, the fire incident was reported to the Bakhshi Ka Talab fire station. Under the direction of the Chief Fire Officer, two fire tenders were immediately dispatched to the scene, led by the In-charge Fire Officer. Upon arrival, the fire had taken a fierce form and was spreading rapidly. Considering the seriousness of the situation, additional fire tenders, including one from Indiranagar, two from Chowk, a water bowser and a Multi-Disaster Response Vehicle from Hazratganj, were called to the scene. All teams surrounded the area and continuously sprayed water, after which the fire was brought under control.

stories.title: Deputy CM visits Varanasi:Prays at Baba Vishwanath and Bankati Hanuman temples; says people must have faith in Ayodhya investigation
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya arrived in Varanasi on Thursday. He first visited Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham and performed darshan of Baba Vishwanath. Varanasi Cantt Assembly constituency MLA Saurabh Srivastava accompanied Maurya during the darshan. The Deputy Chief Minister remained in the temple premises for about half an hour and gathered information from officials about the facilities and security arrangements for devotees in view of the month of Sawan. After darshan at Kashi Vishwanath Temple, the Deputy Chief Minister went to Bankati Hanuman Temple located at Durgakund. Here he had darshan of Pawan Putra Hanuman and prayed for the happiness, prosperity and welfare of the people of the state. Expressed gratitude for the budget announced by PM Welcoming the development projects worth approximately ₹25,000 crore announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Kashi and Purvanchal, the Deputy CM said that this will prove to be a milestone in the development of Kashi and several surrounding districts. Maurya said that he has seen Kashi during the governments of Congress, Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party, and is also seeing today's Kashi, where a wonderful coordination of development, modern facilities and religious faith is visible. Maurya said that today whoever comes to Kashi, truly experiences it as the city of Baba Vishwanath. Deputy CM speaks on Ayodhya offering theft case In response to a question asked about the theft of offerings in Ayodhya, Keshav Prasad Maurya said that this is a sad incident of theft. He said that the police are arresting the accused and investigating the entire matter. Along with this, the SIT is also engaged in the investigation and the truth will come out soon. He said that all people should have faith in the law. Along with this, giving a religious reference, he said that one should also have faith in the mace of Hanuman Ji Maharaj. Takes aim at Akhilesh Yadav On a question asked about a viral poster of Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav, the Deputy Chief Minister launched a sharp attack. He said that Akhilesh Yadav comes from that family whose head was Mulayam Singh Yadav, during whose rule bullets were fired at unarmed Ram devotees in Ayodhya. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav has never shown respect towards Ram, Shiva and Krishna and has ignored the sentiments of Hindu society. Maurya said that whenever Akhilesh Yadav makes such statements or posts, it hurts the sentiments of Ram devotees, patriots and the saint community.
