stories.title: Son shoots father with six bullets:Murder linked to ₹150 crore property dispute; mother says, 'You have destroyed our family'
stories.summary: A son murdered his father over a property dispute worth ₹150 crore in Ghaziabad. According to the police, around 12 AM on Wednesday night, the accused shot his father 6 times in the face, chest, and stomach with a pistol. According to family members, the son had come home after drinking alcohol. The father scolded him, after which he committed the crime. Seeing her husband's dead body, the wife screamed and told her son, “You have ruined the entire house.” After the incident, the accused fled. Family members took Hariom Chaudhary to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police investigation revealed that the son, Nikhil Nehra (32), was pressuring his father to transfer the property into his name. His father, Hariom Chaudhary (52), was not ready for this. He feared that his son would sell the land and squander the money on alcohol. According to the police, about eight years ago, Nikhil had also shot his younger brother Nishu, but he survived. Police have deployed 4 teams to search for the accused. The incident occurred in the Modinagar police station area. 25 bigha land was in son's name Hariom Chaudhary was a resident of Budana village in the Modinagar police station area of Ghaziabad. He was a prosperous farmer. In his name, there is 75 bigha land near Modinagar and a market in front of Jeevan Hospital on the Delhi-Meerut Road. His total assets are estimated to be around ₹150 crore. His family includes wife Anita, elder son Nikhil Nehra, and younger son Nishu. Both sons are unmarried. ACP Bhaskar Verma said that the elder son Nikhil is addicted to alcohol. Because of this, he often had disputes with his father. His father did not like his drinking and used to scold him. He had also given Nikhil shops in the market and 25 bighas of land, but he wanted to transfer the remaining property to his name as well. The ACP stated that on Wednesday night, Hariom Chaudhary had dinner with his wife and younger son. At that time, the elder son Nikhil was not at home. He arrived home late at night after drinking alcohol. According to family members, the father scolded him for coming home drunk. At this, Nikhil pulled out an illegal pistol and started abusing his father. An argument ensued between the two. Hearing the noise, Hariom's wife Anita and younger son Nishu also reached there. During this, a scuffle broke out and Nikhil fired shots at his father. As soon as he was shot, Hariom fell to the floor. Hearing the sound of gunfire, nearby people arrived and took him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. ACP says, ‘Accused will be caught soon’ Modinagar ACP Bhaskar Verma stated that the elder son murdered his father. Family members have mentioned a land dispute. Police are investigating all aspects. A case has been registered against the accused based on the family's complaint. He will be arrested soon.

stories.title: Lucknow sees stormy rain with 50 kmph winds:2-storey house collapses in Noida, funeral held under tarpaulin in Jhansi
stories.summary: The monsoon has once again picked up pace in Uttar Pradesh. Heavy rainfall has been lashing Lucknow since 6 pm on Thursday evening. Strong winds blowing at nearly 50 kmph were also recorded. Several roads across the city were waterlogged. The state capital had also witnessed heavy rainfall in the morning. Rainfall was recorded in more than 15 cities including Barabanki and Jaunpur on Thursday. In Jhansi’s Tahrauli area, people were seen performing a funeral under a tarpaulin amid rain. In Greater Noida’s Tilpata village, a two-storey house suddenly collapsed around 1:30 pm on Thursday afternoon. The house was located near a drain, and its foundation had weakened due to rainfall. Fortunately, no casualties were reported. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 36 districts on Thursday. Rainfall is expected across the entire state on Friday. During this period, thunderstorms and strong winds are also likely. Meanwhile, rising rainfall in hilly regions has started increasing the water levels of rivers in Uttar Pradesh. In Ballia, erosion has begun along the banks of the Ghaghra River. In Bansdih, people are demolishing their own concrete houses and shifting to safer locations. So far, 150 families have left their homes. In Varanasi, three steps of Dashashwamedh Ghat have submerged due to the rising water level of the Ganga. However, the river is still flowing 11.90 metres below the danger mark. In Mathura, the Yamuna River is in spate, with the water level flowing 1.30 metres below the warning level. The steps of Vrindavan’s Keshi Ghat have also been submerged. In Prayagraj, the water of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers has reached shops built along the ghats. Earlier on Tuesday, rainfall was recorded in 40 cities across the state. Meanwhile, since June 1, Uttar Pradesh has received 25% less rainfall than normal. Monsoon likely to intensify from July 17 Rainfall was recorded in 25 cities during the last 24 hours. The highest rainfall of 22.5 mm was recorded in Lakhimpur Kheri. Uttar Pradesh has received 27% less rainfall than required so far. The Meteorological Department said heavy rainfall activity is likely to increase in eastern UP from July 17 and in western UP from the following day. Lucknow senior meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: “A weather system has formed over eastern UP. The monsoon line is passing through the Terai region. Due to this, clouds are present, but most parts of the state are not receiving good rainfall. A low-pressure area formed over the Bay of Bengal is continuously strengthening. It is likely to move towards the northwest in the next 48 hours. Due to its impact, the monsoon will become active again in UP after July 17 and good rainfall is expected.” Funeral performed under tarpaulin amid rain in Jhansi A distressing picture has emerged from Bangri Bangra village in Tahrauli tehsil of Jhansi district, where a lack of basic facilities forced villagers to perform a funeral under a tarpaulin during heavy rainfall. Due to the absence of a tin shed at the cremation ground, the family of a poor man had to conduct his last rites while taking shelter under a tarpaulin. The deceased had reportedly suffered from illness and financial difficulties throughout his life. Even after his death, he could not receive a dignified farewell. During the funeral, family members and villagers had to rely on a tarpaulin to protect themselves from rain. After the video of the incident surfaced, villagers expressed anger against the local administration and public representatives. They said even basic facilities like a tin shed had not been provided at the cremation ground, making an already sensitive process difficult. Villagers have demanded that necessary facilities be provided soon. Latest rain update from Lucknow After dark clouds covered the city, heavy rainfall started in Lucknow. Before the rain, cold winds were blowing at a speed of nearly 50 kmph. People in Gomti Nagar, Para and Kakori areas were seen taking shelter under underpasses to avoid getting drenched. Office-goers waited for the water level to recede before continuing their journey. Kanpur receives heavy evening rain, heat and humidity reduce People in Kanpur suffered due to intense heat and humidity since Thursday morning. Around 5:15 pm, the weather suddenly changed as dark clouds covered the sky and heavy rain started. The rainfall brought relief from the heat and humidity. Before the rain, the maximum temperature recorded in the afternoon was 36.6°C. According to the Meteorological Department, temperatures are expected to fall further after the rain, keeping the weather pleasant for the next few hours.

stories.title: Ram Mandir theft row:Accused Anukalp got close to Champat Rai by reciting poetry; villagers shut doors, refuse to talk
stories.summary: Anukalp had a deep interest in reading and reciting poetry. In 2024, he performed at a Kavi Sammelan in Ayodhya, where the chief guest was Champat Rai, General Secretary of the Ram Mandir Trust. According to people familiar with the matter, Champat Rai appreciated his performance and blessed him by placing his hand on Anukalp's head. That meeting proved to be a turning point. Anukalp reportedly began addressing Champat Rai as "Babuji" and, through those connections, secured entry into the Ram Mandir administration. He was eventually assigned duty in the mandir's cash-counting room. According to the Special Investigation Team (SIT), Anukalp gradually siphoned off crores of rupees from the mandir offerings over a period of time. However, investigators found only ₹16.82 lakh in his bank account. Back in his native Basawan village in Milkipur, his grandfather told Dainik Bhaskar, "It was looting in the name of Lord Ram. He started looting and eventually got caught." Today, the family claims Anukalp's name has become synonymous with disgrace in the village. Village turns its back on Anukalp To understand Anukalp's life before joining the Ram Mandir, the Dainik Bhaskar team visited Basawan village, around 40 kilometres from Ayodhya. The village has a population of nearly 2,000. As reporters walked through its narrow lanes towards Anukalp's house, they found villagers unwilling to speak about him. Several residents got up and walked away when questioned, while others shut their doors. Some even advised the team not to visit his house, saying "nothing good" would come of it. The prevailing mood in the village was one of resentment, with many residents unwilling even to hear Anukalp's name. Grandfather says he never believed his grandson could do this At the family home, reporters met Anukalp's grandfather, Rajendra Mishra, who suffers from a heart condition. Speaking about his grandson's arrest, Rajendra said, "No one tells me what is happening. He is only 18 years old. I don't know why his father sent him to work at the Ram Mandir. I had sent him to Prayagraj for his studies. A few months later, I learnt that he had gone to Ayodhya instead." Asked whether investigators had visited the family, he replied, "Whoever needed to come came and questioned us. We had nothing to hide." When asked how Anukalp secured work at the Ram Mandir, Rajendra maintained, “I don't think Anukalp could do something like this.” Family blames internal feud for Bhagwat Katha controversy Rajendra also spoke about a dispute that erupted during a Bhagwat Katha organised by Anukalp in Milkipur in April 2026. According to him, the incident stemmed from a long-running family dispute. He said he has four sons, with Anukalp's father, Ravindra Mishra, being the eldest. The youngest son, Brijendra, has an ongoing dispute with his wife, Neha. Rajendra alleged that Neha arrived at the religious event with her family members, triggering a commotion. He further accused his brother, Surendra Mishra, of orchestrating the episode. "He called our daughter-in-law Neha there. He never misses an opportunity to defame our family," Rajendra claimed. When asked about reports that expensive sarees worth around ₹10,000 each had been purchased from a trader in Kumarganj for distribution during the event, and that the SIT had questioned the trader, Rajendra dismissed the allegations. "It is all false. I suspect Surendra framed Anukalp," he said. Uncle questions sudden rise in family wealth Rajendra's brother, Surendra Mishra, presented a different version of events. He said Anukalp's father had struggled financially for years and had lived at his maternal aunt's house for four to five years. Anukalp also spent part of his childhood studying there before becoming associated with the Ram Mandir Trust. Surendra said he was surprised when the family purchased a house in Ayodhya worth around ₹40 lakh last year. "I could not understand where so much money had come from," he said before ending the conversation. Conversations with several villagers suggested that Anukalp's family had long remained socially isolated. Residents said Anukalp's father, Ravindra Mishra, contested the village head election twice but failed to secure even 100 votes on either occasion. He also lost the Block Development Committee (BDC) election. When asked about Ravindra's occupation, villagers said he was associated with a government hospital and used to earn some income there. However, none could clearly identify his designation or exact role. Friend says fame and wealth changed him Back in Ayodhya, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to one of Anukalp's friends, who described him as an ordinary young man before joining the Ram Mandir. The friend said Anukalp regularly attended Kavi Sammelans wherever he heard they were being held and often described himself as a social worker. According to the friend, after Champat Rai entrusted him with an important responsibility at the mandir in 2024, Anukalp's lifestyle changed dramatically. Within six months, he bought his father a Maruti Suzuki Swift Dzire. The friend said Anukalp, who previously wore kurta-pyjamas costing ₹400-500, began wearing branded outfits priced between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000. Planned ₹2 crore land investment, wanted to buy Scorpio The transformation extended to his property ambitions. As the 84 Kosi Parikrama Marg was being developed near Basawan village, Anukalp reportedly expressed interest in buying around two bighas of land in the area. Several property dealers attended the Bhagwat Katha he organised, but the proposed purchase did not materialise because a suitable contiguous plot was unavailable. According to people familiar with the discussions, Anukalp told the dealers he was prepared to invest around ₹2 crore in land. In 2025, he also helped his brother-in-law, Lavkush Mishra, secure a job at the Ram Mandir. Thereafter, the two allegedly became actively involved in purchasing property. Investigators have also received information suggesting that Anukalp bought land in Ambedkar Nagar in his father's name. Those transactions are currently under investigation. Sources further claimed that Anukalp had been planning to purchase a Mahindra Scorpio before the alleged mandir donation theft came to light.

stories.title: How to withdraw money from PF:Step-by-step guide; balance transfers automatically after job change, self e-KYC possible; 8 key rules changed
stories.summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has introduced a series of reforms aimed at making Provident Fund (PF) withdrawals faster and simpler. Members can now apply for withdrawals online from home, receive funds within a fixed timeline, and have their PF balance transferred automatically when changing jobs. The latest reforms include eight major rule changes, covering emergency withdrawals, pension, e-KYC, nominations, and digital services. 1. Easier advance PF withdrawals EPFO has classified advance PF withdrawals into three categories: 2. Full PF withdrawal rules revised EPFO has divided members' PF balances into two parts: Employees who have completed at least one year of service can now withdraw their entire PF balance during emergencies. Earlier, members had to remain unemployed for at least two months after leaving a job before becoming eligible for full withdrawal. The entire PF balance, including the protected 25%, can still be withdrawn upon retirement after the age of 55, permanent disability, job loss under eligible conditions, or permanent relocation abroad. 3. EPS withdrawal waiting period increased Under the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), the waiting period for pension fund withdrawal has been extended to 36 months under the new EPS Scheme-2026. Previously, the waiting period was two months. 4. PF claims to be settled within 20 days EPFO has fixed a maximum processing period of 20 days for all online PF claims. If an employer deducts PF contributions from employees' salaries but fails to deposit them with EPFO on time, a 12% penalty will be imposed. The amount will be recovered from the salaries of the responsible officials. 5. Automatic PF transfer after job change Employees will no longer need to submit Form 13 when changing jobs. Under the upgraded system, the employee's Universal Account Number (UAN) will automatically synchronize records between the old and new employer. Once the first Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) is filed by the new employer, the PF balance will automatically transfer to the new account. 6. New process for UAN activation and e-KYC To curb PF fraud, EPFO has overhauled the UAN activation process. Members will no longer be able to activate a UAN directly through the EPFO website. Instead, activation will take place through a new secure interface available only on the UMANG mobile app. Aadhaar-based facial authentication has been made mandatory for activating a UAN. 7. e-Nomination made simpler Earlier, members had to submit Form 2 through their employer or the EPFO office to add nominees. Now, nominees can be added online through the EPFO portal using the e-Nomination facility. Members must also upload a recent passport-sized profile photograph on the portal to complete identity verification. 8. Six-month relief for private PF trusts EPFO has granted a six-month compliance window to private PF trusts that are yet to register under its regulations. Trusts completing registration within this period will receive relief from earlier penalties, interest, and legal proceedings, helping safeguard employees' retirement savings. EPFO 3.0 to further simplify PF services EPFO is also preparing to launch its new EPFO 3.0 digital platform. The upgraded system will enable faster claim settlements, quicker withdrawals, multilingual online services, and an improved user experience. More than 300 million account holders are expected to benefit from the new platform. EPFO said the reforms are aimed at making PF services more accessible while continuing to provide 8.25% annual interest on members' deposits. Members facing technical issues related to UAN activation, e-KYC, or login can contact the EPFO official helpline at 14470.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft- SIT submits report to SC:Hearing to be held tomorrow; Rahul writes to PM Modi, says 'Your silence is unacceptable'
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir submitted its status report to the Supreme Court on Sunday. According to media reports, the report has been filed in a sealed cover. A three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant is scheduled to hear the matter on Monday. Four separate petitions related to the alleged donation theft have been filed before the Supreme Court. During the previous hearing on July 13, the court issued a notice to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust and directed the Uttar Pradesh government to submit the SIT's status report within a week. The Uttar Pradesh government constituted the SIT on June 13 at the request of the temple trust. The team comprises Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, IG Kiran S, and Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan. Meanwhile, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding an independent investigation into the trust's financial affairs. They also called for the trust's accounts to be made public so devotees can know how and where the donations have been spent. They said anyone found responsible during the investigation should be held accountable. The letter, written on Saturday and made public on Sunday, stated: "You announced the formation of the trust in Parliament, but its members were appointed entirely by the government. It is well known that the trust members are associated with the RSS, VHP and their affiliates. The former general secretary was also considered close to you. In such circumstances, your silence is unacceptable. Ensuring accountability is your responsibility. The credibility of both the government and the trust depends on it." Police question main accused and his Nephew Sunday marked the last day of police custody for the main accused, Ramashankar Yadav alias 'Tinnu', and his nephew Manish. On Saturday morning at around 8:30 am, police took both men from the district jail on a 39-hour remand. Officials remained at the SOG office until around 11 pm, and the accused were not taken elsewhere during the remand. Tinnu is said to have been a close associate of former trust general secretary Champat Rai. He was responsible for overseeing the temple's donation boxes, while Manish was involved in counting the donations. Police recovered ₹1 lakh from Tinnu's residence and ₹2 lakh from Manish's house. Earlier, police had also taken six other accused into custody on remand. They have been identified as Avinash Shukla, Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra, Subhash Srivastava, Ramashankar Mishra and Karunesh.

stories.title: Nirmohi Akhada removes Dinendra Das from Mahant post:May also lose Ram Mandir Trust role; Raja Ramchandracharya Das named successor
stories.summary: Nirmohi Akhada has removed Mahant Dinendra Das from his position at the Ayodhya branch. In his place, Raja Ramchandracharya Das Maharaj will now assume responsibility. Along with this, his membership in the Ram Mandir Trust is also in jeopardy. Dinendra Das is an ex-officio member of the Ram Mandir Trust by virtue of being the Mahant of the Ayodhya branch of Nirmohi Akhada. The decision to remove Mahant Dinendra Das from Nirmohi Akhada was taken in a meeting of the Akhada held on July 5. However, this matter came to light on Sunday. The meeting held on July 5 was chaired by Raja Ramchandracharya Das Maharaj, the President of Nirmohi Akhada. In this, allegations were made against Mahant Dinendra Das, including indiscipline, non-compliance with the rules of the Akhada, and concealing important documents. Following this, the sarpanchs and mahants present in the meeting agreed to the proposal to remove him from the post of Mahant. Dinendra Das said - Panches are in my favor; nothing will happen On the news of removing himself from the post of Mahant, Dinendra Das clarified on Sunday. He said, ''Nirmohi Akhada is a panchayati math. Whatever decision the panches take is valid. There are 19 panches in Maharaj Sadan. Out of 19, 13 are in my favor. The remaining 6 are only into politics. Akhada spokesperson Kartik Chopra was earlier our mukhtar (one who has been given authority). I have dismissed him as mukhtar. Kartik is the one talking about removing me. Kartik was doing politics, but he won't be able to do anything. When the panches are in one's favor, nothing will happen.'' CM Yogi was given darshan of Ram Lalla on June 19 After the case of theft of offerings came to light, CM Yogi had reached Ayodhya on June 19 to have darshan of Ram Lalla. At that time, Dinendra Das had arranged the darshan-worship for Yogi. Before this, whenever Yogi reached Ram Mandir, the responsibility of arranging darshan-worship for him was handled by Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao. 5 proposals were passed in the meeting According to information received from sources, a meeting of the Panches of Shri Panch Ramanandi Nirmohi Akhada was held in Delhi on July 5. A total of 5 resolutions were passed in this meeting. One resolution was also to remove Mahant Dinendra Das of the Ayodhya branch from his post. This resolution was proposed by Raja Ramchandracharya Das Maharaj, which was agreed upon by 8 saints. 13 members were invited to the meeting. Of these, 8 members were present, while 4 gave their consent online. However, Mahant Dinendra Das did not participate in the meeting. Questions also raised on Ram Mandir Trust membership Dinendra Das is a member of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust as a representative of Nirmohi Akhada. In such a situation, after the decision to remove him from the post of Mahant, his membership of the Trust is also in danger. It is being reported that Nirmohi Akhada has also filed a new petition in the Supreme Court demanding reconstitution of the Trust. According to the report, Mahant Dinendra Das had said that despite the mention of Nirmohi Akhada in the Supreme Court's decision, he has not been given any important responsibility. He had said that if he gets the responsibility of managing the worship arrangements in Ram Mandir, then he is ready for it. Visits Mandir daily to check arrangements Mahant Dinendra Das had stated that currently the worship and rituals at Ram Mandir are being conducted according to the Ramanandi tradition. He visits the Temple daily to monitor the darshan arrangements. There has been significant improvement in Temple management. The system for counting and depositing offerings has also become more transparent than before. Know who is Mahant Dinendra Das Dinendra Das, who was removed from the post of Mahant of Ayodhya's Nirmohi Akhada, joined the sadhu community at the age of 10. He is also a trustee of the trust that is constructing the Ram Mandir. Nirmohi Akhada was the most important party in the Ram Janmabhoomi legal dispute. That is why he is considered an influential Mahant in Ayodhya. Dinendra Das is the only local resident saint member from Ayodhya in the Ram Mandir Trust. In the year 2019, the Supreme Court delivered a historic verdict in favor of the Ram Mandir. At that time, the court gave special instructions that Nirmohi Akhada should be given representation in the newly formed trust. Under this directive, Mahant Dinendra Das was made a trustee. Currently overseeing the Ram Mandir Trust Significant changes have been made in the Trust after the Ram Mandir donation theft. The entire responsibility of VIP passes and entry arrangements of the Mandir has been entrusted to Mahant Dinendra Das. Earlier, this arrangement was with Champat Rai and Anil Mishra. This means all passes issued for entry into the Temple are being approved only through the digital ID created in the name of Mahant Dinendra Das. Had expressed displeasure over donation theft After the Ram Mandir donation theft case came to light, Dinendra Das openly expressed his anger. He said - Those who tamper with God's offerings should not be forgiven. They should receive strict punishment like the death penalty. He assured that Ramlala's gold and silver ornaments are completely safe. Now know about Nirmohi Akhada... Nirmohi Akhada is the main Bairagi Akhada of the Ramanandi Vaishnav sect. It has been one of the most important parties in the Ram Janmabhoomi dispute in Ayodhya. Due to this, it has played a major role in the Ram Mandir movement and the legal battle fought in court. Currently, Nirmohi Akhada also has representation in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, with Mahant Dinendra Das being a member on its behalf.

stories.title: 'Pay me half my salary, transfer me':IAS officer who performed sit-ups writes to government following Jalaun slapping row
stories.summary: UP IAS Rinku Singh Rahi has once again refused to back down. He has written a six-page letter to the Principal Secretary, Appointment and Personnel Department, in which he has demanded that he be given responsibilities like his other batchmates. If he is not eligible for this, then he should be transferred to another state. Until the order comes, he should be given only half-day's salary, reads Rinku's letter. Rinku is currently posted as Joint Magistrate in Orai, Jalaun. Rinku had a dispute with BJP leader and Block Pramukh Ramraja Niranjan on 23 June. Rinku had gone to inspect the BJP leader's 'Betwa Ice and Cold Storage', where Rinku had slapped Niranjan's mobile and pushed him. Later, he was transferred from Jalaun to Orai. Now read what Rinku Singh wrote in the letter “It will not be possible to continue the job,” according to the letter shared on Facebook IAS Rinku Singh expressed his anguish by posting a letter on Facebook. He wrote, “Good governance and less work means less salary. A colleague compared my situation to a volcano. Just as continuous turmoil goes on inside a volcano, a huge amount of lava keeps forming, but only a small part of it is visible outside; similarly, my struggle against the mismanagement within the system continues mostly uninterrupted and only a small part of it comes out publicly.” “One reason for this is also that there are very few people within the system who accept (not even talking about walking) my walking on this path of struggle. Perhaps they have fear for themselves or their close ones that someone might come and stop the fulfilment of their greed from the government system. Or there is an ego that says they are no less honest and dutiful than anyone else. Whereas most people outside the system will either not understand these internal administrative struggles, or will get confused, or will consider it a waste of time. Therefore, only as much is shared publicly as is necessary and appropriate in the public interest,” he said. “In this context, at the persistent request of well-wishers, I am sharing one of my letters. Perhaps this letter may provide an answer to the question - what exactly do I want to do? Will the common people benefit from my struggle/fight? And why do I face similar circumstances and problems at almost every place? Will I be able to deliver any output in my lifetime (whereas the reason for zero output is that no one believes that this can happen. However, if there is even a discussion on good governance, a lot of output will come.... if some work gets done, then politics itself will improve).” “To those colleagues or senior persons who advise me from time to time that why don't I compromise like others and get the work done, my humble request to them is that please accept one thing about me - if there is no good governance (basic governance), then it will not be possible for me either to do this job in a normal manner.” Big statements by Rinku Singh Rahi... 1- I will not take salary without work “While holding the current post of SDM (Judicial), I get only about four hours of work in a day. When I am not able to work to my full capacity, the government can give half salary if it wants. I should be posted at a place where I can work according to the rules. If there is no such place in Uttar Pradesh, then posting them in another state should also be considered.” He called the DM's public hearing programme a show and said that it hurts his inner soul. He said that spending time with the DM in public hearing is like deceiving oneself. 2- Salary continued without responsibility In the letter, Rinku Singh mentioned the incident that occurred in Shahjahanpur, in which a video of him doing sit-ups in front of lawyers had surfaced. He wrote, “After this incident, he was kept attached to the Revenue Council for about a year, due to which he continued to receive salary without any responsibility.” He said that this was against his moral principles. Later, at his request, he was posted in Jalaun. 3- Created WhatsApp groups for good governance Rahi claimed in the letter that to establish good governance in Jalaun, he created separate WhatsApp groups for each gram panchayat and locality. Officials, employees, and common citizens were added to these groups so that transparency and public participation in administrative work could be increased. He said that through these groups, social audit of the actual presence and work of gram panchayat secretaries, lekhpals, sanitation workers, and other field employees became possible. This brought to light corruption and irregularities in many cases, and common people also submitted complaints and suggestions with evidence. 4- Accused of not sharing important information Rinku Singh also alleged in the letter that despite repeated requests, much important administrative information was not made available in these WhatsApp groups. These include daily attendance of Lekhpals, Gram Panchayat Secretaries and other field staff, pending work and information related to daily tasks performed. He says that making such information public could have further strengthened transparency and accountability in administration. 5- ‘Not being allowed to work’ Rinku Singh alleged in the letter that during action on cases of illegal occupation and encroachment in Jalaun tehsil, he faced obstacles at administrative and other levels. He has mentioned Cabinet Minister Swatantra Dev Singh and Jalaun BJP MLA Gauri Shankar Verma in his letter. In the letter, he has alleged that while serving as SDM in Jalaun, he was given instructions not to take action in some cases of illegal occupation and encroachment. He also wrote that impartial investigation of cases linked to some influential people was affected. Actually, on June 22, a fire broke out in a building in Lucknow, in which 15 young people died. After this incident, while serving as SDM Jalaun, Rinku Singh Rahi had inspected Ramraja Niranjan's cold storage. During a 10-minute fire mock drill, no fire extinguishing arrangements could be initiated in the cold storage in any way, and a report was sought on this. Documents related to cold storage operations were also not available. Rahi claims that after this entire sequence of events, even before the investigation committee's report came, he was transferred to the post of SDM (Judicial). Know who Rinku Singh Rahi is... Resident of Hathras, first became PCS, then IAS Rinku Singh Rahi was born on 20 May 1982, in Hathras, in a Dalit family. He is a resident of village Uswa in Sasni police station area. The elder of two brothers, Rinku's father, Saudan Singh Rahi, used to run a flour mill to support the family. Due to the weak financial condition of the family, Rinku studied in a government school. After passing 12th with good marks, he received a scholarship. With its help, he completed B.Tech from Tata Institute in Jamshedpur. In 2004, Rinku Singh passed the PCS examination. During his job, he appeared for the UPSC Civil Services examination through the disabled quota. In 2021, he secured 683rd rank and became an IAS officer. In the family, his wife, Sulekha, has been a yoga teacher. He has a 10-year-old son named Dhruv Rahi. His uncle Raghuvir Singh Rahi was the district president during the BSP regime. 7 bullets were fired for exposing corruption After becoming a PCS officer, Rinku Singh's first posting in 2008 was as District Social Welfare Officer in Muzaffarnagar. There, he had exposed corruption occurring in scholarships and pensions. Rinku had told Dainik Bhaskar, “In the investigation, I found out that ₹100 crore had been embezzled. Behind this, apart from a political party, there was an entire gang.” At that time, there was a BSP government. On March 26, 2009, Rinku was playing badminton with a colleague. Just then, two attackers opened rapid fire on them. Rinku Rahi was hit by seven bullets. Of these, two hit his face. His jaw came out, and his face was disfigured. Additionally, one ear was damaged, and he lost vision in one eye. Stayed in hospital for a month, staged a sit-in protest After this attack, Rinku was taken to a Higher Centre in Meerut. He remained admitted in Subharti Medical College, Meerut for about a month. He returned after recovering from the operation. After this, Rinku had sought some information from the department under RTI to expose the scam. However, even after a year, he was not given the information. After this, on March 26, 2012, Rinku Rahi started a hunger strike outside the Lucknow Directorate. The police picked up Rinku Rahi from there and sent him to a Mental Hospital in Lucknow.

stories.title: 'I have no regret over my husband's death':Damini says he was having an affair; claims she befriended a van driver because he allegedly assaulted her
stories.summary: A 30-year-old woman arrested for allegedly getting her husband killed through a snake bite in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut told police she had no regret over his death, claiming he was abusive and was having an extramarital affair. During interrogation, the accused, Damini, said she planned the murder after reading about a similar snake-bite case and searched Google for the most poisonous snake before arranging the crime with the help of snake charmers. Police said Damini was sent to jail on Saturday after being produced in court. Investigators are verifying her claims about her husband's alleged affair and have also found over 2,000 phone calls and chat records between her and her boyfriend. The investigation is ongoing. Now read what wife Damini told during police interrogation... Police: How did you meet Tushar? Damini: Tushar came to the school asking for a van driver job. We hired him. He used to bring children to school in an eco van and drop them off. He also used to pick and drop me from school to home. We started talking in the van itself. After a few days, we became friends. Then gradually I became closer to him. We had been in a relationship for about 1 year and wanted to get married. Our plan was that after Atul's murder, Tushar would also divorce his wife. Because he was also having disputes with his wife. Police: If it was a love marriage with Atul, then why did you want to kill him? Damini: I had a love marriage with Atul 7 years ago. He loved me very much, but 2 years after marriage, that love ended. He started beating me over every little thing. In 2022, I found out about his affair with another woman. I myself did not want to live with him. I had filed an application at the SP office for divorce from Atul. Then the family members convinced me and called me back. I had also filed a complaint with the Women's Commission. Police: From where and how did you bring the snake? Damini: When I told Tushar about the plan to get my husband bitten by a snake, he also agreed. For 3 months, we searched for snake charmers. Then we hired snake charmers Sonu and Uday. Tushar had given 15 thousand rupees to the snake charmers on July 7. The deal was finalised with them for 5 lakh rupees. The snake was locked in a box and hidden in the school itself. Police: How did you commit the murder? Damini: On July 16, when Atul came home, we had dinner together. I gave Atul milk with 12-15 sleeping pills mixed in it. After that, Atul fell asleep. At 5 AM on July 17, I called Tushar. Tushar, Sonu, and Uday came to the house quietly. They released a snake on Atul's bed in the sheet and left. The snake was pressed under the sheet. The snake bit Atul. Then I started making noise. I called my in-laws and told them that a snake had bitten my husband. He is unconscious; please come quickly. Police: How were you so sure you would escape after the murder? Damini: In Ravita's case, they had strangled her and left a snake on the bed. Later, the strangulation came to light in the post-mortem. The snake that Ravita had left on the bed was also not venomous, which is why she got caught. That's why we decided that we must bring a venomous snake, so that it would appear in the post-mortem that she was bitten by the snake itself. We were sure that no one would be able to guess our conspiracy and we would escape. Police: What was the plan after the murder? Damini: After Atul's murder, we were to get his medical insurance of 20 lakh rupees. After a year or six months, everything would have become normal. Then Tushar and I would have gotten married. We hadn't thought about how and where to get married yet. I would have continued running the school, and Tushar would have been with me. The 36 bighas of land in Atul's name would also have come to my son and me. Police: Didn't you think about what would happen to your son? Damini: I wanted to keep my son with me, because I love my son Manik very much. I had already decided with Tushar that I would not leave my son. When both of us get married and start a new life, son Manik will stay with us. Police: Which astrologer told you to stay away from home? Damini: There were frequent quarrels at my in-laws' place too, which made me unhappy. To get away from all this, I first started living separately with Atul. I had lied to my in-laws that an astrologer had said that I should stay away from family for 4 years. Everything would become fine. After this, she started living separately with her son and husband in a rented house. Both of them started managing the school together. I was the principal of the school, but I looked after the entire management. I used to admit students, teach children as well. I did all the work in the school myself. Still, Atul used to beat me at home. He was the director in the school. Tushar first told the truth to the police Damini's boyfriend Tushar is also married. After coming to Damini's house and releasing the snakes, Tushar came to his own house. As soon as the day broke, he sent his wife and children to his in-laws' place in Shastrinagar. Not only this, Tushar reached Damini's house again after the murder. He went there and started crying and wailing. Tushar was also in a hurry to take the body for the last rites. He was at the forefront. But when Tushar saw that the police had arrived and there was talk of postmortem and investigation, he quietly fled from there. The police reached Tushar's house through surveillance, where it was locked. However, the police arrested him by the night of July 17 (Friday). Know who all are there in both families

stories.title: Akhilesh backs Azam's university in letter to students and parents:Says those without children cannot understand the pain
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has joined the campaign to save Mohammad Ali Jauhar University of Azam Khan, who is imprisoned in Rampur jail. He wrote an open letter addressed to students and parents on X on Sunday at 1:51 PM. The SP president accused the BJP government of politics of revenge. He said, “Those who have neither family nor children, what do they know about the pain of families?” Akhilesh said, “SP is with you in the campaign of youth and their guardians to save Jauhar University. The BJP is burning with the feeling of revenge. The government should not try to make Jauhar University a victim of its narrow politics. Against this malicious, biased decision, we have with us our smallest worker, supporter, biggest leader and also those thousands of children and their parents. The government is trying to run a bulldozer over the dreams of children.” Former minister Azam Khan's Jauhar University has had 38 out of 40 buildings declared illegal. The maps for these buildings were not approved. The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) has ordered the demolition of the university on July 15. The university has been given 15 days before the bulldozer action begins. Akhilesh's 3 major points 1- Must save the temple of education Akhilesh wrote, “Every university is a temple of education. We appeal to the entire country to join us in saving this 'temple of education'. Children from every community study in the university. Has the BJP now turned against the youth of every community? It is the BJP's arrogance that is making them do all these wrong things.” "If there are any paperwork deficiencies, then complete the paperwork to save the university and the students' future," he said, adding, “Poor children study here, who don't have enough money to send their children to expensive universities or abroad as BJP members do.” “If BJP had even an iota of sympathy for children, youth, their families and society, it would immediately find an alternative to this destructive action full of cruelty and injustice.” 2- BJP is against education Akhilesh further wrote, “The truth is that BJP is against education, because educated people are aware and progressive. They also raise their voice against injustice and ask questions, which does not suit the oppressive BJP with its regressive thinking at all. That's why BJP members and their associates keep making underground plans to close down primary schools and even universities in every village.” “BJP members know that after getting educated, people will demand jobs and employment, which the BJP government does not want to give at all. Job recruitment is not in the BJP's agenda. When our primary schools were closed, our vigilant well-wishers foiled the BJP conspiracy by opening 'PDA Pathshala'. That's why now universities have come in their crosshairs,” Akhilesh wrote. 3- This is an extremely disgusting conspiracy by BJP associates and companions This attack on Jauhar University is an extremely disgusting conspiracy by BJP associates and companions against students of every community. All their unregistered schools and educational institutions are running, but a conspiracy of one-sided action is being hatched with a spirit of revenge against others.

stories.title: Block chiefs become administrators in UP:Government bars major decisions, pradhan appointments still pending in court
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has, for the first time, appointed all 826 block chiefs as administrators after doing the same for gram pradhans and district panchayat chairpersons. The Yogi Adityanath government issued the order on Sunday afternoon, marking the first such move in the state's history. According to the Panchayati Raj Department, the first meeting of the current block chiefs was held on July 20, 2021, and their five-year tenure ends on Sunday. With the new order, they will continue as administrators and will be allowed to handle only routine administrative work. They will not be authorised to take any policy decisions independently. Any proposal involving policy matters will have to be sent to the state government through the District Magistrate (DM), with the final approval resting with the government. Sources said the government will soon issue detailed guidelines clarifying the powers of block chiefs as administrators, including which works they can carry out independently and which will require prior approval from the District Magistrate. High Court had questioned appointment of gram pradhans as administrators On June 26, the Allahabad High Court expressed strong displeasure over the delay in holding panchayat elections while hearing a petition challenging the appointment of gram pradhans as administrators. A bench led by Justice Siddharth Nandan asked the state government how it had appointed gram pradhans as administrators, observing that the move appeared to violate an earlier division bench order and could amount to contempt of court. The High Court said gram pradhans could not be allowed to continue as administrators. It noted that the government orders dated May 25 and May 26, 2026, which sought to extend the tenure of gram pradhans, had already been declared unconstitutional. The court also termed the postponement of panchayat elections unconstitutional and directed the government to file an affidavit along with the OBC reservation report and a timeline for conducting the elections. However, it did not grant any interim stay. The petition was filed by Arvind Rathore of Saharanpur. The court fixed the next hearing for July 13 and warned that if the government failed to provide a satisfactory response by then, the concerned official would have to appear in person.

stories.title: Boyfriend kills nurse by injecting poison:Wrote suicide note and planted poison pills to escape arrest
stories.summary: After the murder of a husband by a snake bite in Meerut, now a sensational case of murdering a staff nurse by administering a poisonous drip has come to light. To get rid of his girlfriend's pressure for marriage, the wardboy lover conspired to commit murder along with his friend. On Saturday afternoon around 2 pm, under the pretext of administering a glucose drip, poisonous chemicals were injected. To make the murder look like suicide, the accused wardboy himself wrote a suicide note and placed sulfas tablets in the girlfriend's pocket. The case is from MCC Hospital located on Hapur Road. After matching CCTV footage, mobile records and the handwriting of the suicide note, police arrested the accused wardboy and his friend late at night. The cannula, syringe, mobile phone, fake suicide note, notepad and poisonous chemical found at the scene have been sent for forensic examination. According to police, the nurse's husband had died a year ago. She had been having an affair with the wardboy for about eight months. The girlfriend was continuously pressuring him for marriage. Now read the complete case 26-year-old Neha, a resident of Brahmpuri, was a staff nurse at MCC Hospital located on Hapur Road. Neha got married about 2.5 years ago but her husband Ravi died a year ago. Neha also had a one-year-old son. On Saturday morning around 10 am, she left her son at home and reached the hospital for duty as usual. Around 3 pm in the afternoon, her body was found in a room of the hospital. The hospital administration informed the family members about the incident. When family members arrived, they were informed that Neha's death occurred due to consuming a poisonous substance. However, the relatives denied the suicide claim and accused the hospital management of murder. Following this, there was a major commotion at the hospital. Upon receiving information, the police reached the spot. Brother-in-law said she was killed by poisoning Neha's sister-in-law, brother-in-law and other relatives alleged that the hospital management is hiding the true information about the death. Neha's brother-in-law alleged that she was killed by giving her a poisonous substance. After the relative's complaint, the police started an investigation. Investigation started by seizing CCTV footage CO Kotwali Sangram Singh reached the hospital with the police team. The police seized CCTV footage and started questioning doctors and staff. The police formed two teams to crack the case. During investigation, evidence of continuous conversations between Neha and Suresh was found on Neha's mobile phone. Suresh was also seen leaving the ward in the CCTV footage. After this, the police took him into custody and interrogated him, during which he confessed to the murder. She was pressuring her married lover to marry her During police interrogation, Suresh revealed that he is married and has a 5-year-old son. He had been in a romantic relationship with Neha for the past eight months. Neha had joined MCC Hospital about nine months ago. Neha was pressuring him for marriage, but he did not want to get married. That's why he plotted her murder. He took help from his friend Farhan in this incident. Attempt to mislead police Suresh told the police that after reaching duty on Saturday, Neha complained of dizziness. On this, he admitted her to the ward and called his friend Farhan. After this, he mixed a poisonous chemical in the drip and administered it to Neha. After the poisonous chemical entered her body, Neha died within a short time. After the incident, both of them placed a fake suicide note and sulfas tablets in Neha's pocket, so that the case would appear to be a suicide. After this, both of them left the hospital. Two accused arrested - CO CO Kotwali Sangram Singh informed- Suresh had mixed a poisonous substance in the drip with the help of his friend Farhan. To make the murder look like a suicide, a fake suicide note was created and left at the scene. The police have arrested both the accused. Both have confessed the entire truth.

stories.title: Lucknow school van driver arrested for rape:Sobbing minor identifies accused, recalls abuse
stories.summary: A four-year-old girl studying in nursery was raped by a school van driver in Lucknow. On Saturday, the girl fell ill. When her parents took her to the hospital, the ghastly crime was revealed. When the mother asked the child, she narrated her ordeal. Later, the family reached the police station with the girl, and the police immediately caught the accused and brought him to the station. Upon seeing him, the girl became frightened and started crying. Pointing towards the accused, she said, “Uncle did bad things.” The police registered a case and arrested the accused, Girish Mishra. The incident is from a private school in the Talkatora area of the capital. The accused is a resident of Unnao The girl's parents live in Rajajipuram. They have jobs in the private sector. The mother said, “A van was arranged to take our daughter to and from school. The van was driven by Girish Mishra from Unnao. When the daughter came home from school on Friday, she was frightened. Her health was also not well.” “At that time, I did not pay much attention. On Saturday, the girl's health deteriorated further. She had a fever along with stomach pain. I took my daughter to the hospital along with my husband. The doctors' examination revealed that the girl had been raped. Hearing this, we were shocked. When asked, the daughter named the van driver,” she said. Accused confesses to the crime The accused has confessed to his crime during police interrogation. Girish Mishra said he did wrong acts with the girl while making children sit and get down from the van. He has been working as a driver for 20 years. He has driven vehicles for different institutions at different places. Inspector Kuldeep said- A case has been registered under POCSO Act and rape sections based on the victim's mother's complaint. The accused Girish Mishra has been locked up in custody. It is being investigated whether he has committed any wrongdoing with any other child. Children who travel in his van are being questioned. School staff will also be interrogated. The girl has been admitted to the hospital for treatment.

stories.title: Rahul writes to Modi over Ram Mandir donation theft:Says silence is unacceptable, seeks trust accounts be made public; Tinnu questioned again today
stories.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and party president Mallikarjun Kharge have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the alleged theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir. They have sought an independent probe into the trust's financial affairs and demanded that its accounts be made public so every devotee can know how and where the donations were used. They also said anyone found responsible in the investigation must be held accountable. The letter, written on Saturday, came to light on Sunday. Addressing the Prime Minister, they wrote: "You had announced the formation of the trust in Parliament, but its members were appointed entirely by the government. It is well known that the trust members are associated with the RSS, VHP and their affiliates. The former general secretary was also considered close to you. In such a situation, your silence is unacceptable. It is your duty to ensure accountability. The credibility of both the government and the trust depends on it." Meanwhile, Sunday is the last day of police custody for the main accused, Ramashankar Yadav alias 'Tinnu', and his nephew Manish. On Saturday at around 8.30 am, police took both men from the district jail on a 39-hour remand. Police personnel remained at the Special Operations Group (SOG) office until 11 pm, and the accused were not taken anywhere else during the remand. Tinnu was considered a close aide of former general secretary Champat Rai. He was responsible for overseeing the temple's donation boxes, while Manish was involved in counting the offerings. Police recovered ₹1 lakh from Tinnu's house and ₹2 lakh from Manish's residence. Earlier, police had also taken six other accused — Avinash Shukla, Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra, Subhash Srivastava, Ramashankar Mishra and Karunesh — into custody for questioning on remand.

stories.title: 'DM sir, my uncle locked our house, please open it':Child reaches Lakhimpur tehsil alone, says SHO acts only for commission
stories.summary: In Lakhimpur Kheri, UP, a 13-year-old child reached out to the District Magistrate (DM) all by himself. Seeing this, the DM conducting a public hearing called him closer. When asked the reason for coming, the child boldly said, "My uncle and aunt have forcibly occupied my house and locked it. Please get it opened." The station officer interjected, “We will get it opened.” To this, the child replied, “Not ‘will get it opened’... please get it opened. So I don't have to come again and again.” At this point, the police personnel started laughing. This upset the child. He said, “What do you people care, if you just get your commission, you work rapidly.” DM Anjani Kumar Singh told Kotwal Rajesh Kumar, “Go to the child's house and get the lock opened.” The Kotwal immediately reached the spot. Upon inquiry, it was found that the house which the child was talking about getting opened belonged to his father's first wife. The first wife had passed away. His son lives in Lucknow. The child's uncle has locked the room. After this, the Kotwal returned without getting the lock opened. The matter is from Saturday afternoon. The DM was conducting a public hearing on Samadhan Diwas at Sadar Tehsil. Its video has surfaced today. The child's name is Amitabh Gupta. Read the conversation between the child and the DM Child- DM sir, my uncle and aunt have occupied our house. Please get the house lock opened. We are very poor. DM- Who is the Station House Officer? This child studies in class 7th. Child (interrupting the DM)- Not 7th, in 8th. DM (laughing)- This child studies in 8th standard. Has come alone. See what his problem is. Sadar Thana In-charge- We will get it done. Child (looking at Sadar Thana In-charge)- Not "will get it done", please get it done. Child (to DM)- Sir ji, tell the Station House Officer to get the lock opened. So we don't have to come again and again. Sadar Thana In-charge- Come, will get it opened right now. Child- What do you people care, if you just get commission then all work gets done quickly. (Everyone laughs loudly at the child's remark.) DM- How old are you? Child- 13 years old. DM (explaining to the child) Right now you leave everything and focus only on studies. Child- We want to study, but there are many difficulties. When mom goes to the market, she only brings vegetables worth ₹50. What can you get in ₹50 worth of vegetables? There is such poverty in our house that we don't even have enough to eat. DM- Does mom bring vegetables for cooking or for selling? Child- For cooking. But what can you get in ₹50 worth of vegetables for four people? DM (explaining to the child again)- Look, leave everything else aside for now and just focus on your studies. Sometimes when you talk too much, the other person feels bad. Things get spoiled. Child (interrupting the DM again)- Sir ji, can I ask one thing? Right now my elder sister and I are studying, but what about later? How will we manage the expenses of education? DM- Education is free. Notebooks and books are all free. Child- And when my sister goes to 9th grade later? DM- Your mom does some work, doesn't she? Child- Yes, they do labour work. But in today's date, what can be done with ₹3,000. DM- You just focus on your studies. We will show you. Know why the child wants to get the lock opened Amitabh's father Harish Gupta has four brothers. A few years ago, all the brothers separated. In the division, the other three brothers got one room each, while Harish got two rooms. The police investigation revealed that Harish is mentally unwell. He has married twice. The son of the first wife, whose mother has passed away, lives with his aunt in Lucknow and studies there. Amitabh claims that the room that was allotted to his father in the partition now belongs to him, because the first wife has died and their son does not live here. Mother said, “He had left saying he was going to school” The child's mother told the police that her son is not interested in studies and often keeps roaming around. “He had told me he was going to school to get his TC (Transfer Certificate) processed, but he reached the tehsil and lodged a complaint there,” she said.

stories.title: Mini-van rams two bikers to death in Varanasi:Duo were talking next to parked bike, flung far away after collision
stories.summary: Two men were killed and one was seriously injured after a speeding mini-van hit them in Varanasi on Saturday night at 9.30 PM. Upon receiving information about the incident, Raja Talab Police reached the location. With the help of local people, all three victims were taken to Heritage Hospital located on the highway. There, doctors declared two young men dead. The condition of the third is critical. His treatment is ongoing. All three young men were friends. The incident occurred in the Raja Talab area. The bike was stopped, a speeding magic hit it Jamal (26) and Shahid (20), residents of Birbhanpur in Raja Talab, were friends. Both were riding on a Bullet motorcycle on Friday night heading towards Raja Talab. Jamal's uncle Jahangir said that on the way, near the petrol pump in front of Birbhanpur-Odar village, Jamal and Shahid stopped after seeing their friend Amin. Meanwhile, a speeding goods-carrying Magic vehicle came from the Jansa side and collided with the stationary bike. According to eyewitnesses, the collision was so severe that the bike was thrown up in the air and all three youths were flung about five metres far. Police have taken the Magic vehicle and its driver into custody. The bodies of both deceased have been taken into custody and have been sent for post-mortem. Police are investigating the causes of the accident. Footage from CCTV cameras installed nearby is also being examined. Relatives reached the hospital crying and wailing As soon as the news of the incident was received, the relatives of the deceased reached the hospital. The relatives were in a terrible state, crying inconsolably. There is mourning in the village. A large number of people are reaching the homes of the deceased to express their condolences. A wave of grief has spread across the entire area. Jamal's uncle Jahangir has filed a report against the errant mini-van driver.

stories.title: Woman who got husband bitten by snake cries for son:Tossed turned in Meerut jail, hid face when asked why; brother said ‘she is dead’
stories.summary: The woman accused of orchestrating the murder of her husband by allegedly getting him bitten by a snake spent a sleepless night in Meerut jail, repeatedly asking to see her six-year-old son, according to sources. During police questioning, Damini (30) reportedly broke down as investigators asked when and how she had planned the killing of her husband, Atul Kumar (32). On Saturday, the Dainik Bhaskar team travelled to Hastinapur, about 40 km from the crime scene, visiting the homes of Atul, Damini and her alleged lover, Tushar Payla. While Damini's brother disowned her, saying she was ‘dead’ to the family, Atul's brother demanded the harshest punishment for the accused, saying he believed justice would be served. Bhaskar team visits Tushar's house The Dainik Bhaskar team first reached the home of Tushar Payla, the school van driver and alleged lover of Damini. His two-storey house is about 1.5 km from Damini and Atul's Krishna Kids School. Neighbours call him from a 'Good family' A neighbour said Tushar's family had been living there since 1982 and described them as ‘a very good family’. She said she could not believe Tushar could be involved in such a crime. According to residents, the family has been missing since Friday morning, and the house has remained locked ever since. House found deserted A grey Eco van, which Tushar allegedly used daily to transport schoolchildren, was parked outside. Although the main gate was latched but not locked, no one responded after repeated knocks. Inside the premises, the team found a black car with a Delhi registration bearing the words ‘Tushar Payla, District President, Gurjar Sangh’. A buffalo shed stood in front of the house, while a dry hand pump was installed on one side. Rooms locked, uncle refuses to speak The team went upstairs and found two rooms, both locked from the outside, with an open terrace at the rear. Later, they visited Tushar's uncle, who was sitting outside his house with a neighbour. He declined to comment, saying, 'We don't know anything, and we don't want to talk about it.' Team reaches Damini's maternal home After visiting Tushar's house, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached the maternal home of accused Damini, located about 800 metres from Krishna Kids School in a densely populated neighbourhood. Damini had earlier run a cosmetics business from the house. Family distances itself from Damini Neighbours and family members initially refused to speak to the media. A relative who came out of the house said the family had severed ties with Damini after her marriage. He said, We don't want to speak to anyone. We don't know what she did, why she did it or at whose behest. Brother says, 'She is dead to us' While the team was outside, three young men arrived on a motorcycle. They objected to the media presence and asked Damini's brother, Sonu, to go inside. After requesting the camera be switched off, Sonu said, We have nothing to do with Damini. You can ask the police if you want. When we learnt about Atul's death on Friday, we were the first to demand a post-mortem. Whether she remains in jail or does anything else, it makes no difference to us. For us, she is dead. School remains shut after murder case After leaving Damini's house, the Dainik Bhaskar team visited Krishna Kids School, which Atul and Damini ran from a rented building. The school, located on the main road, was locked. Signboards outside still displayed the names MD Atul Pawar and Principal Damini. Neighbour recalls daily routine An elderly man sitting outside said the couple had rented the building from a local Brahmin family. Around 100 to 150 children and several teachers attended the school every day. He said Tushar regularly transported the children in his van and would often wait outside the school. 'Tushar often arrived with Damini' The man said Tushar was frequently seen dropping off and picking up Damini in the school van. ‘We saw them together many times, but never asked any questions,’ he said. The school has remained closed since Friday morning. No children or parents have visited since the incident, and locals said they have no information on when it will reopen. Family mourns at Atul's ancestral home After visiting the school, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Atul's ancestral home, about 3 km away. A steady stream of relatives and neighbours continued to arrive as the family mourned. Atul's parents, elder brother and other relatives were present, while women of the family wept inside the house. Relatives said they were satisfied with the police investigation and had nothing more to add. 'Damini rarely visited our home' Atul's elder brother, a retired soldier, said Damini called him at around 6 am on Friday, informing him that Atul had been bitten by a snake. He said, When we reached their rented house, Atul had already died. He said Atul and Damini had a love marriage and belonged to the same community. The couple had been living in a rented house with their six-year-old son. While Atul visited the family regularly, Damini rarely came to the ancestral home. 'We have faith the killers will be punished' The brother said the family did not know Tushar or the reasons behind the alleged dispute between Atul and Damini. He said, We trust the police investigation and have faith in the law. Those responsible have been arrested, and I believe the killers will receive the death penalty. 'Atul's son will stay with us' Asked about the couple's son, he said the child was at his grandmother's house and asleep inside. 'He is still very young and doesn't know what has happened,' he said. On who would raise the child, he replied, 'He is Atul's son and belongs with us. We will look after him.' When asked what would happen if the maternal family sought custody, he said, "After marriage, this became his home. The child is ours, and we will raise him." stories.title: Rivers swell across UP, two houses washed away:Ghats submerged in Prayagraj; rain hits Lucknow and 25 cities
stories.summary: The monsoon has once again intensified across Uttar Pradesh, with rainfall reported in 25 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur and Bareilly, since Sunday morning. Several other parts of the state are witnessing cloudy weather. Agra was plunged into darkness during the day due to thick cloud cover. A rain alert has been issued for all 75 districts of the state, with heavy rainfall expected in 31 districts. Meanwhile, rivers across Uttar Pradesh are in spate. In Ballia, the Saryu river has reached close to the danger mark, posing a flood threat to around 100 villages. Erosion continues along the riverbanks, with one house being washed away into the river within five seconds. In Lakhimpur, a house collapsed into the Sharda river due to erosion. Fortunately, no one was inside the house at the time. In Kanpur, the Ganga river has reached the warning level, prompting authorities to ban boating. In Varanasi, the steps of Dashashwamedh Ghat have been submerged due to the rising water level. At the Sangam in Prayagraj, announcements are being made asking people to stay away from the river. The Yamuna water level is also rising in Mathura and Vrindavan. Earlier on Saturday, rainfall was recorded in 25 cities, including Bareilly and Agra. Gorakhpur received 110 mm of rain in six hours, turning roads into ponds. Water entered lanes, colonies and several houses. The OPD section of the district hospital was also flooded. A boy died after drowning in a pit filled with rainwater. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: “The monsoon has become active again in Uttar Pradesh. Due to the low-pressure area formed over the Bay of Bengal and the movement of the cloud system towards Jharkhand, monsoon winds have shifted towards Uttar Pradesh. This has triggered the return of rainfall. The weather is expected to remain the same until 24 July. Some areas in the southern parts of the state may witness heavy rainfall.”

stories.title: Vaishnavi trolled over ‘Krishna Nikkama Nakaara’ poem:Gained attention with Ashutosh Rana; says she reads her father’s poems
stories.summary: “Come Bharat! Sit for a moment, I will tell you what's in my heart, On this throne of Raghuvansh, I want to see you seated.” Young poetess Vaishnavi Sharma begins the dialogue in the role of Mother Kaikeyi. From the other side, the pain of Ashutosh Rana playing Bharat is heard- “Mother...what have you done? You have extinguished the lamp of the family.” Vaishnavi, who delivered Kaikeyi's dialogues in the Bharat-Kaikeyi conversation, was highly appreciated for her powerful presentation. She said, “I recite poems written by my father Satish Sharma from the stage. However, on social media, people often understand the meanings of poetic lines partially or incompletely. She added, "The same thing happened while reciting a poem written on Shishupal Vadh. It had lines- Krishna is Nikamma (useless) and Nakara (worthless), black, illiterate and completely boorish;His attire is like a forest dweller, filled with deceit inside and out;His parents are unknown, there is no record of his lineage or clan;He steals butter from house to house, who knows what they see in him. As soon as the video surfaced, there was an uproar. People started trolling. They were not ready to believe that these words were said by Shishupal to Shri Krishna." She further said, “It was after this that Shri Krishna killed Shishupal.” Then Vaishnavi Sharma's poem 'Kupit Yajnaseni' based on Draupadi's disrobing became popular. It was viewed by 3.4 million people on her YouTube channel. Read the complete interview Question. How do you introduce yourself? Vaishnavi. My name is Vaishnavi Sharma. I was born in Lucknow. My father Satish Srijan is in the Army, he writes poetry. I present his poems on stage with the accompaniment of flute and classical ragas. Due to Army background, we lived in different places. The advantage of this was that we kept learning and adopting the culture of different places. Question. Your real name is Vaishnavi Sharma, but on stage you are known as Raag Vaishnavi? Vaishnavi. My real name is Vaishnavi Sharma. Actually, in classical singing there are Raag Durga, Raag Saraswati, Raag Bhairavi, but Raag Vaishnavi was not found. That's why we created YouTube and Instagram accounts with this name. People started knowing me by this name. More than 2 lakh people on YouTube and more than 90 thousand people on Instagram have connected with me. Question. What attracted you most towards language, poetry and Indian philosophy? Vaishnavi. First credit goes to my Army background. Having gone to and lived in so many places, all this has a great impact on the mind. I got to hear a lot about Urdu literature from my grandfather. My grandmother's principal was Mahadevi Verma. We have been hearing about her since childhood. My father has studied Hindi literature. Apart from all this, dialogue and contemplation have been very important in our family. What I heard in childhood, I am seeing all that as I grew up. All the credit goes to my family members. Question. You often say from various platforms that we want to make Hindi cool for the youth? Vaishnavi. Hindi is cool, I know that. I also know that many people don't know this. When I went to study at Delhi University, I saw that many people couldn't even write in Hindi. They use Roman script for English. When I saw all this, it occurred to me that these people shouldn't be deprived. That's why I want to connect everyone with it. Besides, just as every photo has a negative, similarly every culture also carries a negative with it. Question. Your most popular performance is 'Kupit Yajnaseni'. How did you bring it to life? Vaishnavi. Kupit Yajnaseni is a poem based on Draupadi's disrobing. We present it on stage with Raag Dhanashri and Raag Tillu. This poem essentially explores faith. Like when Draupadi was dependent on her husbands, arguments and counter-arguments were going on. Finally she lost. Then she remembered Krishna. That is, she had faith in him and Lord Krishna saved her. One thing to say about Kupit Yajnaseni is that we created it to save in the archive, then it got shared. Many people shared it. My friends would send me videos and ask, 'Look, is this you?' I would tell them yes, it's me... Question. Has any interesting incident happened in a live show? Vaishnavi. Nothing like this has happened to me live, but it has definitely happened on social media. I had presented a poem on Shishupal Vadh. Actually, Shishupal had hurled 100 abuses, and Shri Krishna kept forgiving him. As soon as the 101st abuse was hurled, Krishna killed Shishupal. I had recited a poem on this context of Shishupal's 100 abuses. People edited and presented it in a distorted manner. It appeared as if I myself was abusing Shri Krishna. Question. What projects are you working on? Vaishnavi. I have been doing stage shows for the past 4 years. Before that, I used to do theatre and such. There are also some songs now, which will come out later. Question. Would you like to work in films or web series? Vaishnavi. I have worked in the film industry. I wrote dialogues for the Tamil web series 'The Journey'. Actually, all its shows are in Tamil only. There was one Hindi episode, in which we wrote the dialogues. Question. If you could make one improvement in the Indian art world, what would you do? Vaishnavi. In my life, the art factor is being handled by my father. I feel that being too purist about language causes harm. This deprives the language of its nourishment. By doing this, we all made Sanskrit an elite and distant language. It became distant from common people. Now only those who are studying it speak and read Sanskrit. We don't want Hindi to face the same situation. However, this doesn't mean at all that the dignity of the language should be degraded.
