stories.title: How Jauhar University led to Azam Khan's political downfall:Huge donations, alleged land grabs; if anyone asks for an account, he replies with 'I don't know'
stories.summary: The university that Mohammad Azam Khan once considered the biggest symbol of his political influence has now emerged as one of the biggest reasons behind the collapse of his political career. The dream, which began 32 years ago with a small library named Jauhar, culminated in the establishment of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in 2006. However, a series of legal disputes, allegations of land grabbing, and administrative action have since placed both the university and Azam Khan under intense scrutiny. How 'Azam' became a politician Jailed during emergency, emerged as leader after his release Mohammad Azam Khan was born on 14 August 1948, exactly one year after India's Independence, to Ameer Jahan and Mumtaz Khan in a middle-class family. During the 1970s, he studied at Aligarh Muslim University, where he became popular among students for his command of Urdu. During the Emergency imposed by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Azam openly criticised the government and was jailed. Following the end of the Emergency, he entered active politics. He lost his first election in 1977 but won the Assembly election in 1980 as a Janata Dal (Secular) candidate, becoming an MLA at the age of 32. He later represented Lok Dal, Janata Dal and Janata Party. When Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the Samajwadi Party (SP) in 1992, Azam Khan became one of its founding members. He continued winning elections on the SP ticket and was inducted into the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet in 2003. During this period, he pursued his long-standing dream of establishing a university in the name of freedom fighter Mohammad Ali Jauhar. He created the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and frequently spoke about building an educational institution dedicated to Jauhar's legacy. University dream brought him down Those who refused to give land allegedly kept at police station In 2006, Azam Khan invited Mulayam Singh Yadav to lay the foundation stone of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. Around 78 hectares (nearly 300 bighas) of land were acquired for the project. While some farmers in Aliyaganj voluntarily parted with their land, many opposed the acquisition. Local residents alleged that circle rates in the area had deliberately been kept nearly 33 per cent lower than neighbouring areas. In 2019, residents of Aliyaganj filed a case against Azam Khan, alleging that their land had been forcibly acquired. Villagers claimed that police personnel would take residents to police stations and keep them there until they signed land transfer documents. They also alleged that even minors were picked up on some occasions. University built on 38 hectares of government land When the SP returned to power in 2012, dream was fully realised The return of the Samajwadi Party to power in 2012 revived construction at Jauhar University. The amended legislation was passed and the university was granted private university status. Azam Khan became its Chancellor for life. As one of the most influential ministers in the government, he secured significant funding for the university. The Jauhar Trust also received substantial donations. Two mosques were constructed inside the university campus, and nearly ₹550 crore was spent on developing the institution. Admissions began, and classes commenced. At one stage, more than 3,000 students were enrolled. However, after the BJP formed the government in 2017, investigations into the university began. When questioned by the media about the source of funding for the university, Azam Khan repeatedly said he did not know. Asked about the construction of the mosques inside the campus, he again responded that he did not know who had built them, remarks widely viewed as sarcastic. During the 2019 Lok Sabha election campaign, Azam Khan targeted then District Magistrate Anjaneya Singh during a roadshow. He referred to government officials as salaried employees and remarked that, after the election, he would make the District Magistrate clean his shoes. Following the statement, it was widely believed that the Uttar Pradesh government gave Anjaneya Singh a free hand to pursue investigations against Azam Khan. Subsequent inquiries examined schools, colleges, and land linked to him. Four Rampur Public Schools allegedly built on illegally occupied land were sealed between 2019 and 2023. Azam's politics finished Lost MLA membership after conviction in fake birth certificate case University can be saved by paying ₹100 cr On 15 July 2026, the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) ordered the demolition of 38 of the 40 buildings inside Jauhar University after finding that their building plans had not been approved. To challenge the order, Azam Khan would now have to approach Anjaneya Singh, the same officer whom he had once publicly referred to as a ‘paid employee’. Anjaneya Singh is currently Commissioner of the Moradabad Division and also serves as Chairman of the Rampur Development Authority. Even if Azam Khan challenges the demolition order in court, approval of the building plans would still have to come from the RDA. According to an RDA official, obtaining approval would now require payment of nearly ₹100 crore, including development charges, compounding fees, impact fees and other levies. The official said that had the building plans been approved before March 2026, the total cost would have been only ₹5–6 crore, as Singankheri village was then under the Zila Panchayat and came under the Rampur Development Authority only in March 2026.

stories.title: Register an e-FIR from anywhere:File on your mobile, valid for court insurance claims; police station visit required only in specific cases
stories.summary: Has your mobile been stolen? Has your bike disappeared? Or has an online fraudster siphoned money from your bank account? For such minor complaints, there is no need to go to the police station anymore. You can file an online FIR (e-FIR) from your mobile or computer while sitting at home. Learn the step-by-step method to file an online FIR, legal rules, and what rights you have if the police refuse Online FIR can be filed from home in these cases According to UP Police rules, you can file an online FIR in cases where the accused is unknown and no serious physical violence has occurred. For example, if your car, bike, scooter, bicycle, or any other vehicle has been stolen. If your mobile phone, laptop, or tablet is stolen from the market, bus, train, or anywhere else. If your Aadhaar card, PAN card, passport, school-college mark sheet, or driving license is lost. Someone might have broken the lock of your house or shop, but you don't know who did it. Money might have been deducted online from your bank account. Your Facebook-Instagram account might have been hacked, or someone might be blackmailing you on the internet. Online FIR valid in both 'Court-Insurance' Many people have the misconception that a document will not be considered official until it has the police station's stamp and the inspector's signature. But, that is not the case. Under the Information Technology Act (IT Act) and the Indian Evidence Act, a digitally certified and generated e-FIR has the same legal status as a regular FIR. If your vehicle is stolen, this online copy will be valid for getting a claim passed by the insurance company. It is also legally acceptable for re-issuing a lost SIM card or passport. What to do if an online FIR is not heard? If the local police hesitate to act on your valid complaint, the country's law gives you 3 strong options. 1. Appeal to the SP or SSP: You can send your complaint in writing to the Superintendent of Police (SP) or Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) of the district via post/speed post. You can also meet them directly at their office. 2. File a complaint on the Jansunwai portal: You can file a complaint against the police department by visiting the UP government's Jansunwai portal jansunwai.up.nic.in. This portal is directly monitored by the Chief Minister's Office (CMO). Therefore, local police have to respond within a stipulated time. 3. There is also the option of going to court: Even after this, if there is no hearing, you can apply through a lawyer in the court of the regional magistrate under Section 156(3) of the BNSS. If the court feels that the matter is worthy of investigation, it reprimands the police and immediately orders the registration of an FIR and action. These complaints filed online fall under the NCR category. Let's also understand the difference- NCR stands for Non-Cognisable Report. It is filed in less serious cases. For example, mutual verbal abuse, minor assault, loss of mobile or wallet, bike theft. In such cases, the police cannot directly investigate or make an arrest. The permission of a magistrate (court) is required before starting an investigation. FIR stands for First Information Report. It is filed in serious or legally actionable crimes. For example, robbery, cyber fraud, murder, or dacoity. As soon as an FIR is filed, the police can start an investigation without the court's permission. If necessary, they can also arrest the accused.

stories.title: BJP MLA rebukes electricity department employee:'If you keep drinking like this, how will you work?'; asks DM, 'Are officials here just to sleep?'
stories.summary: BJP MLA Ketki Singh reached Revati Power House in Ballia at 11 PM on Friday. She got angry seeing the SSO in an intoxicated state. She said - When you drink so much, how will you work? You can't even speak properly. When the woman MLA called the XEN and SE, their phones were switched off. The JE did not receive the call three times. Angered by this, she called the DM. She asked him, ''Are the electricity department officers meant to sleep at home? When the public sleeps, only then will the officers sleep.'' This video of Ketki Singh surfaced on Saturday. Read the complete incident step by step... Bansdeeh MLA Ketaki Singh reached Rewati on Friday. Here, she held a meeting with workers at around 7:30 PM. During this, workers complained to her about power cuts. Ketaki Singh attended a feast program at 9:30 PM. From there, she reached Rewati Power House directly at around 11 PM. A lock was hanging on the gate there. As soon as news of the MLA's arrival was received, SSO Ranjit alias Pintu Singh reached the spot. He opened the lock of the power house gate. The MLA reached inside with the workers and sat on a cot. She asked the SSO why there was no electricity in the area. After this, she called for the log register and checked it. During this, Ketaki Singh scolded the SSO, saying, ‘When you drink so much, what work will you do? Not a single sound is coming out of your mouth.’ MLA told DM- I am sitting at the power house MLA Ketaki Singh called the DM and informed, I am sitting at Revati Power House. I had a program here today. People are surrounding me and complaining that there has been no electricity for 4-5 hours. When I called, the XEN's mobile was switched off. Are they switching off their mobiles to sleep in their homes? 'When the public sleeps in electricity, only then will the officers sleep' The MLA said common people will stay on the streets with fans; officers will switch off their phones and sleep. People in Rewati have been troubled for four days. If the lights don't come on in the town area today, all officers will have to sleep without electricity. When the public sleeps in electricity, only then will the officers sleep. The government is providing 18 hours of electricity, but the officers are putting on a drama. SSO said - People abuse when lights go out The MLA told the SSO - There should be no complaints again. Fix a time when there will be no electricity. Then people will prepare accordingly in advance. If there is no electricity all night, how will they sleep? The SSO clarified - When someone's electricity goes out, people come here and start abusing. BJP MLA Ketki Singh said, ''I am with the public in all their joys and sorrows and will continue to be. The government is providing 18 hours of electricity in the humid heat.'' Despite this, employees are unable to supply electricity. The SE and XEN's mobiles were continuously switched off. That's when I had to talk to the District Magistrate.

stories.title: Deputy CM touches woman's feet at hospital:Asks, "Amma, what's the problem?"; tells CMS, 'No need to fold your hands'
stories.summary: Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak reached Kashi's government hospital on Saturday around 6 pm. He directly interacted with patients and attendants. During this, the Deputy CM sat down on the floor next to an elderly woman. He inquired about her well-being. Then, while getting up, he touched the woman's feet. The Deputy CM asked, "Amma, what is your problem?" To this, the woman said, "My daughter is admitted to the hospital. My health is also not well." After this, the Deputy CM reached the Chief Medical Superintendent's (CMS) cabin. The CMS started answering his questions nervously with folded hands in front of the Deputy CM. On this, the Deputy CM said, "Doctor Sahab, don't fold your hands; it doesn't feel good. You are a senior doctor." See 3 pictures... Now, know the complete matter The matter is of Shri Shivprasad Gupta Divisional Hospital. Here, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak inspected for about half an hour. He asked several patients about the hospital arrangements. The Deputy CM directly reached the emergency ward. Here in the waiting area, elderly woman Taramuni was sitting on a chair. Seeing the elderly woman, Pathak turned towards her. Without delay, he sat down near the woman's feet. He said, 'Mother, is there no inconvenience here?' Have you been asked to get medicine from outside in the hospital? Are you comfortable now?' Taramuni answered all his questions with 'yes'. After this, Pathak touched the elderly woman's feet and went straight inside the general ward. Expressed displeasure over AC not working When the Deputy CM reached the ICU of the emergency ward, he looked at the AC and asked - Why is this not running? He gave immediate instructions to the superintendent to get the AC running. Actually, the AC was running, but there was no cooling. Reached the shivering patient, said - why wasn't she given a blanket The Deputy CM reached the bedside of a woman admitted in the general ward. She was being given oxygen and was shivering. The woman was lying on the bed without a blanket. On this, Brajesh Pathak immediately asked to give her a blanket. Similarly, he inquired about the condition of 2 other patients as well. He gathered information about the arrangements from caretaker Pooja Giri. He asked, ''Are any medicines being prescribed from outside? To this, the patients informed him that they are receiving medicines from inside only.'' CMS got nervous seeing Deputy CM After the inspection, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, after touring the entire general ward, went straight to the cabin of Chief Medical Superintendent Dr. Brajesh Kumar. He inquired about the hospital arrangements for about 15 minutes. Sitting beside him, Superintendent Dr. Brajesh Kumar was nervously answering his questions with folded hands. Upon this, he said, ''Don't worry, answer comfortably. We are all family.'' CMO could not answer Deputy CM's questions After this, Brajesh Pathak reached Pandit Deendayal Government Hospital. He expressed displeasure over the lab built here not being operational. When he asked CMO Mukesh Kumar the reason for this, he could not answer. He started looking towards Additional Director Dr. N.D. Sharma sitting beside him. On this, Brajesh Pathak instructed the Additional Director to inspect the hospital at night. Find out and tell us why the lab has not been able to start yet? Brajesh Pathak also inquired about the Multi Superspeciality Hospital being constructed at Kabir Chaura Hospital. He instructed officials to work day and night to complete it. He also gave instructions to the executing agency for this. He said, ''Until the hospital is ready, the patients of this hospital should be shifted to the women's hospital located next door. So that no patient faces any inconvenience in treatment.'' Department is alert regarding Corona On Corona cases being found in Varanasi, he said that there is no need to panic. The patients who have been found have no problems. They have been kept in home isolation. The department is fully prepared regarding this. During Brajesh Pathak's inspection, Mayor Ashok Tiwari, MLA Saurabh Srivastava, AD Health Dr. N.D. Sharma, Dr. Satyen Rai and others were present.

stories.title: Gorakhpur rain turns into trouble:Roads to markets waterlogged, 110.2 mm rainfall recorded in 24 hours
stories.summary: Around 110.2 mm rainfall in the last 24 hours once again exposed the poor drainage system of Gorakhpur city. The rain that started on Friday afternoon continued till late night and remained intermittent from early Saturday morning. After continuous rainfall, several major roads, markets and low-lying areas of the city were submerged. With several feet of water accumulated on roads, people found it difficult to step out of their homes. Those heading to offices, schools, colleges and other essential work on Saturday morning faced waterlogging and traffic jams at several places. Waterlogging in many areas of the city After the rain, waterlogging was reported in areas including Town Hall, District Hospital Road near Ghosh Company, School Road in Civil Lines, Gandhi Gali, Rapti Complex, CMO office premises, Alinagar, Asuran, Mohaddipur and other low-lying areas. Water remained accumulated for hours at several places, making it difficult for people to even walk. Residents of low-lying areas found water collected outside their homes, while several shops were affected due to waterlogging in front of their establishments. CMO office also not spared The CMO office premises also could not escape waterlogging after the rainfall. Water accumulation inside the office campus caused difficulties for patients, attendants and employees. During this time, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak, who arrived for an inspection, reviewed the situation. He said that waterlogging occurs at the CMO office because the land is located in a low-lying area. Officials have been instructed to find a permanent solution soon. Vehicles crawled on the roads The city’s traffic system was also badly affected due to the rain. Two-wheeler riders faced the most problems on water-filled roads. Several bikes and scooters broke down midway, while cars were seen moving at extremely slow speeds. The risk of accidents increased due to potholes hidden under the water. Long queues of vehicles were seen on several major roads, and commuters took much longer than usual to reach their destinations. Problem occurs every year The heavy rainfall has once again raised questions over the preparedness of the Municipal Corporation. Local residents said that the same situation occurs every monsoon. Due to delayed cleaning of drains and lack of proper drainage arrangements, even a short spell of heavy rain leaves the city waterlogged. At several places, drains overflowed, causing dirty water to spread onto roads. Residents said the problem of waterlogging returns every year, but a permanent solution has still not been found. Difficulties increased for children, patients and working people The waterlogging affected common people the most. School-going children had to cross waterlogged roads to reach their schools. Patients and their families visiting hospitals also faced severe difficulties. At several places, e-rickshaw and auto drivers refused to enter waterlogged routes. The accumulation of dirty water has also increased the risk of infectious diseases. Highest rainfall in July since 2021 Meteorologist Dr Kailash Pandey said that the monsoon has performed well in Gorakhpur this year. Around 260 mm rainfall has been recorded in July so far, which is the highest for the month since 2021. However, the normal rainfall figure for July is 383.4 mm, and the city is still short by around 123 mm. If rainfall continues in the coming days, there is a strong possibility that the normal rainfall mark will be achieved by the end of the month. Heavy rainfall expected in coming days as well The Meteorological Department has predicted that the monsoon will remain active in eastern Uttar Pradesh for the next few days. Intermittent moderate to heavy rainfall is expected, with heavy showers likely at some places. Officials said that if the drainage system is not improved immediately, the waterlogging problem in low-lying areas may become more severe. While good rainfall has brought relief to farmers and raised hopes of better crops, for city residents, waterlogging with every spell of rain is becoming the biggest challenge.

stories.title: Shiv Sena seeks namaz ban at Gyanvapi during Sawan:Shinde faction urges CM Yogi to consider devotees’ demand, sends memorandum
stories.summary: Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) has sent a memorandum to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath demanding a ban on namaz at the mosque located inside the Gyanvapi premises in Varanasi during the month of Sawan. The party said that a large number of devotees visit the Kashi Vishwanath Dham during Sawan, and special arrangements should be made while keeping the religious sentiments of Hindus in mind. Requests CM to issue directions Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) spokesperson Om Prakash Mishra said that earlier on July 15, a memorandum regarding the same demand was submitted to the district administration. Now, an appeal has been made to the Chief Minister to issue necessary directions to the district administration so that action can be taken on the demand. Shiv Sena demands ban on namaz throughout Sawan Om Prakash Mishra said that the party has demanded a temporary ban on the entry of people offering namaz in the Gyanvapi mosque, located adjacent to the Baba Kashi Vishwanath temple complex, throughout the month of Sawan. He claimed that the move would respect the religious sentiments of devotees and help ensure smooth arrangements during the holy month. He said, “All of us get the opportunity to have darshan of Maa Shringar Gauri only once a year. Therefore, our demand is that namaz should be restricted throughout Sawan.”

stories.title: Azam’s sentence upheld over ‘Clean my shoes’ remark:To serve 2 years in jail for threatening an IAS officer during polls
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, who had made controversial remarks saying, “These collectors and officials are salaried employees…,” has received a major setback from a Rampur court. The district court has upheld the decision of the MP-MLA court. Azam Khan was sentenced to two years in jail in this case on May 16. Azam had challenged the MP-MLA court’s order in the sessions court through an appeal. The hate speech case dates back to the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, when Azam Khan was the Samajwadi Party-Bahujan Samaj Party alliance candidate from Rampur. However, in the case related to objectionable remarks against four district officials, Azam Khan has been acquitted by the court. What Azam Khan had said Azam Khan had said: “Everyone stay firm, do not fear the collector or other officials. They are salaried employees, we are not afraid of them. I have seen many pictures of Mayawati, where big officers kept taking out handkerchiefs and cleaning shoes. We have an alliance with them, and I will make them clean shoes too… if Allah wishes.” In 2019, Anjaneya Kumar Singh was the District Magistrate of Rampur, who is currently the Moradabad Divisional Commissioner. On his instructions, Tanda SDM Ghanshyam Tripathi had registered a hate speech FIR against Azam Khan at Bhot police station. The court delivered its verdict in the case after six years. Faisal Lala had appealed against acquittal in officials’ remark case In the case related to comments against four officials, Faisal Lala had filed a case at Rampur Kotwali on April 2, 2019. After the hearing, the trial court acquitted Azam Khan in the case on December 18, 2025. Fifteen days later, Faisal Lala filed an appeal against the verdict in the sessions court. He had demanded that Azam Khan should be punished in the case. Azam Khan and his son Abdullah are currently lodged in Rampur jail. The court had sentenced both of them to seven years in prison in the fake PAN card case. On Saturday, Azam Khan appeared in the court hearing through video conferencing. Now read the case related to remarks against four officials During the 2019 Lok Sabha election campaign, Azam Khan had made a controversial statement at the party office. Referring to the then District Magistrate, Additional District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate and City Magistrate, he alleged that the four officials had come from a district where poor people were “melted with acid” and that they now wanted to bathe Rampur in blood. The officials against whom Azam Khan made allegations included: Anjaneya Kumar Singh, then District Magistrate of Rampur (currently Moradabad Divisional Commissioner) Jagdamba Prasad Gupta, then Additional District Magistrate (now retired) PP Tiwari, then Sub-Divisional Magistrate (died after retirement) Sarvesh Kumar, then City Magistrate (currently Municipal Commissioner in Moradabad)

stories.title: Devotee dies on boat at Prayagraj Sangam:Collapses suddenly while using phone; family had come from Mathura
stories.summary: A 38-year-old devotee died of a heart attack while visiting Sangam in Prayagraj. A video of the incident, which took place on July 15, surfaced on Saturday evening around 5 pm. The video shows the devotee sitting on a boat wearing a life jacket. He was using his mobile phone, while a child was sitting in front of him. Suddenly, the devotee collapsed and could not get up again. He had come to visit Sangam with his family from Mathura. His cousin Ranveer Thakur is the Mathura BJP district minister. See 2 pictures... Entire family had come from Mathura to visit Prayagraj Vishnu Thakur was a resident of Barsana in Mathura. He ran a guest house. His cousin Ranveer Thakur is the Mathura BJP district minister. Ranveer said, “On July 15, the entire family had gone from Mathura to take a dip at Sangam. Vishnu, his wife Hemlata, his sister and brother-in-law, and his brother and sister-in-law were among those who had travelled.” The family reached Sangam at around 4:30 pm and boarded a boat to go towards Sangam Nose. Vishnu was sitting near the edge of the boat. His brother and other family members were sitting beside him. His five-year-old nephew was sitting in front and playing. Fell while sitting on the boat, then didn't get up As the boat moved ahead, Vishnu suddenly fell over while sitting on the boat. Initially, the family members could not understand what had happened. Later, when they tried to wake him up, they found him unconscious. The boat was immediately taken back to the ghat. The family rushed him to a nearby hospital, but doctors there referred him elsewhere. He was then taken to another hospital, where doctors declared him dead. What does the video show? A 21-second video of the entire incident has surfaced. It shows Vishnu Thakur sitting on the boat with his family. A few seconds later, he suddenly collapses. People present on the boat become frightened and try to help him. A woman’s voice can be heard from behind saying, “What happened to him?” Other family members can also be heard asking the boatman to stop the boat. According to the family, Vishnu was using his mobile phone moments before the incident. After Vishnu’s death, the family took the body back to Mathura. His last rites were performed on July 16. Meanwhile, the Daraganj police denied having any information about the incident. Station House Officer Gyaneshwar Mishra said that no such information had been received by the police station.

stories.title: Murder accused arrested after 27 years of killing 2 cops:Faked death as Bhura, lived in Bhopal as Jameel
stories.summary: The main accused in the murder of two policemen in Agra 27 years ago has been arrested by police from Bhopal. To escape police action, the accused had got himself declared dead. However, police got a clue about him recently through a Bakrid feast. After this, police laid a trap and arrested the accused. Accused was active member of Ramesh Kushwaha gang DCP West Aditya Kumar said the arrested accused Bhura was an active member of the Ramesh Kushwaha gang. The gang was involved in robbery, kidnapping and murder cases. Police had earlier seized a large cache of weapons belonging to the gang. Ten days later, on the night of December 31, 1999, the gang planned to rob police personnel to recover weapons. Bhura arrived in a jeep along with gang leader Ramesh and eight other associates. Three policemen deployed for patrolling in Kheragarh were warming themselves near a bonfire due to the cold. Bhura and his associates also sat near the fire on the pretext of warming themselves. Taking advantage of the opportunity, Bhura shot all three policemen with a country-made pistol. One policeman died on the spot, while another died during treatment. Constables Kamal Singh and Charan Singh were killed in the incident. Gang members killed, others sentenced to life imprisonment In the case, police killed Ramesh Kushwaha in an encounter in Bhind and Narendra in Jalaun. Five other criminals were arrested and later sentenced to life imprisonment. To escape from police, Bhura fled into forests and worked as a labourer in Itarsi for two months. Later, he started working in building construction in Bhopal and eventually became a truck driver. After this, accused Bhura, son of Sabu and a resident of Jaitpur, got himself declared dead. He continued working as a truck driver in Madhya Pradesh and changed his identity to Jameel, son of Farooq. Bakrid feast helped police track accused Recently, a conversation between Bhura’s brother-in-law and one of his former gang associates, who had been released from jail, took place during a Bakrid feast. During a liquor party, the associate revealed that he had spoken to Bhura two years ago. This information reached Station House Officer Harish Kumar. Police then laid a trap and arrested the accused. Initially, Bhura tried to mislead the police, but after strict questioning, he confessed his identity. DCP West Aditya Kumar said the accused has been sent to court. He will be taken on remand for further questioning.

stories.title: VIDEO | Car runs over 3-year-old, child dies:Driver allegedly on phone; brother carries body in his arms
stories.summary: A three-year-old child was crushed by a car in Prayagraj on Friday afternoon at 12:39 pm. The child had reportedly lain down on the road after insisting on something. At the same time, a car coming from behind ran over him and moved ahead. The accident took place around 200 metres away from Jhunsi police station. A CCTV footage of the incident has also surfaced. The footage shows that the car continued moving without applying brakes even after running over the child. Eyewitnesses claimed that the driver was talking on the phone at the time of the accident. However, police have not officially confirmed this. An FIR has been registered against the unidentified car driver. Police said they are trying to identify and trace the car and its driver with the help of CCTV footage. See 3 pictures... Know the complete case Rajkumar, a resident of Chamanganj area of Jhunsi, lives with his family near Green Park. He has three sons. Rajkumar works as a daily wage labourer. On Friday afternoon, his three-year-old son Abhishek was going to collect water from a nearby tap along with his two brothers. While walking near the petrol pump in front of Green Park, his two brothers moved ahead, while Abhishek lay down on the road out of stubbornness. At that moment, a car coming from behind ran over him. The car’s wheel passed over the child’s head, due to which he died on the spot. The family rushed him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Entire incident captured on CCTV The entire incident was recorded in a CCTV camera installed at a nearby grocery shop. The footage shows three children walking on the service road. While playing, one child lies down on the road. At the same time, a car moving around 10 metres behind him runs over him without slowing down. The driver neither applied brakes nor stopped the vehicle after the accident. After the incident, another child coming from behind rushed to the spot, lifted injured Abhishek and moved him to the roadside. Hearing the commotion, nearby residents and school students also gathered at the spot. Driver being traced based on CCTV footage: Inspector After the incident, an FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station on the complaint of the family. Jhunsi Inspector Mahesh Mishra said, “Police are searching for the driver based on the CCTV footage. The police team is conducting raids. The body has been sent for postmortem.”

stories.title: 'Babua woke up at noon, held gatherings in evening':Yogi takes dig at Akhilesh in Bulandshahr, says Ram has left him unable to act
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday said the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress had neither vision nor sensitivity and accused governments before 2017 of exploiting people and turning Uttar Pradesh into a BIMARU state. Targeting SP chief Akhilesh Yadav again, Yogi said, "Before 2017, 'Babua' used to wake up at 12 noon. By 2 pm he would get dressed, and by 5 pm it was time to go to the gym. After returning, if time permitted, he would sit with his gathering. Where was the time to think about the public, farmers, the poor, women or traders? He did nothing for the people earlier, and Lord Ram has now left him with nothing to do." Yogi is on a visit to Bulandshahr, Amroha and Sambhal on Saturday. He began his tour by laying the foundation stone for 20 development projects worth ₹574.56 crore and inaugurating 24 completed projects in Bulandshahr. Read the key points of CM Yogi's speech... 1. 'Previous governments had no vision, 29 sugar mills shut' The Chief Minister said the SP and Congress governments before 2017 lacked vision, time, sensitivity and the will to work. "We are working for the people because we are committed to them. Between 2007 and 2017, 29 sugar mills shut down in Uttar Pradesh. Industrial development came to a complete standstill. Worshippers of Jinnah only exploited the people and turned Uttar Pradesh into a BIMARU state. After the double-engine government came to power in 2017, the wheel of development started moving again," he said. 2. 'SP decided who would get government jobs' Yogi said development under the double-engine government now reaches everyone without caste-based discrimination and recruitment is fully transparent. "When vacancies are announced, youths from every section get jobs. Before 2017, however, SP and Congress ministers, along with goons patronised by them, took money to decide who would get jobs. Every district had a parallel mafia government. SP-backed criminals had turned every district into an extortion hub. Which district was left untouched by riots? Remember the Bulandshahr Cantonment incident before 2017 and the objectionable statements made by SP ministers. They had no concern for the people," he said. 3. 'Daughters were unsafe, traders feared leaving home' The Chief Minister said women were not safe before 2017. "A trader leaving home prayed that he would return safely to see his family again. Today, under the double-engine government, there are no curfews and no riots. Everything is fine in Bulandshahr. We have delivered on our promises. We said we would reduce the mafia to dust, and we did. We also said those who endanger the safety of daughters have only two destinations—jail or hell. There is no third option," he said. 4. 'We must repay Bulandshahr with development' Yogi said development becomes visible only when people elect good public representatives. "Bulandshahr has done us a favour. You ensured our victory in both Lok Sabha seats and all Assembly seats. Whether Bulandshahr raises its voice or not, we have to continue development here. We have to repay the debt we owe to the people of Bulandshahr. Keep blessing us, and we will turn the vision of Ram Rajya into reality," he said. 5. 'Jewar Airport will drive western UP's economy' The Chief Minister said Jewar International Airport would become a new centre of industrial growth in Uttar Pradesh. "The airport has begun operations. It will become the foundation of industrial development not only for western Uttar Pradesh but for the entire country. Spread over 14,000 acres, it will emerge as a major hub for aircraft maintenance, cargo movement, domestic and international air services," he said. 6. 'UP has moved from the bottom three to the top three' Yogi said Uttar Pradesh was once identified by its poor roads. "Earlier, people knew they had entered Uttar Pradesh the moment they saw potholes on the road. Today, the Ganga Expressway is built to global standards. People can travel from Meerut to Lucknow in four hours. That is the speed of development and prosperity. Uttar Pradesh is now among the country's leading states in several sectors. Fifty-five per cent of India's mobile phones are manufactured in Uttar Pradesh, along with 60 per cent of electronic appliances. The state also ranks first in ethanol production. Before 2017, Uttar Pradesh was among the bottom three states. Today, it has moved into the top three," he said.

stories.title: Priest murdered at 50-year-old Hanuman temple:Throat slit, body dumped on steps; had served there for 20 years
stories.summary: A 55-year-old priest was brutally murdered with a sharp weapon at a 50-year-old Hanuman temple in Uttar Pradesh's Mahoba district. His throat was slit and his blood-soaked body was dumped on the temple steps. The body was discovered around 11 am on Saturday when devotees arrived to offer prayers. They informed the police. The priest had been living at the temple and performing daily rituals for the past 20 years. The incident sparked panic in the area. Police and forensic experts reached the spot, collected evidence and sent the body for postmortem. The Circle Officer said an FIR has been registered on a complaint filed by the priest's elder brother. Police said the accused would be arrested soon. The incident took place in Kulpahar police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters. Used to live alone in Hanuman temple According to police, priest Udit Narayan Mishra (55), a native of Amgaon in Hamirpur district, looked after the Hanuman temple in Jaitpur Belatal village of Mahoba. Jaitpur Belatal has a population of around 25,000 Hindus and 8,000 Muslims. The priest lived alone in the temple and was unmarried. On Saturday morning, villager Kapil reached the temple for darshan and found Mishra's body lying at the entrance. Villagers said - He had no enmity with anyone The priest's younger brother, Jugal Mishra, reached the spot after receiving the information. He said, "We were three brothers. Our eldest brother died long ago. Udit was the second among us. Around 20 years ago, he renounced worldly life and moved from Hamirpur to Mahoba. He used to visit home occasionally and stayed in touch over the phone. He had no enmity with anyone." Local residents described the priest as a calm and humble person. They said he conducted daily prayers and devotional singing every morning and evening, and had never been involved in any dispute during the past 20 years. Police said- Investigation started after collecting evidence Additional SP Vandana Singh said police reached the spot immediately after receiving information about the murder and collected evidence. She said the initial investigation suggests the murder may have stemmed from a personal dispute. There were no signs of theft or vandalism. Police suspect the priest was deliberately targeted and killed. Further investigation is underway.

stories.title: Former SP MP says Ram, Krishna could be Muslim prophets:Remarks follow cleric's claim Krishna offered namaz five times a day
stories.summary: After a cleric claimed that Lord Krishna was a Muslim, former Samajwadi Party MP ST Hasan has said that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna could have been among Islam's 1.24 lakh prophets. Speaking in Moradabad, he said, "Many Muslim scholars believe that Lord Ram and Lord Krishna may have been among the 1.24 lakh prophets." He added, "Many things change over such a long period, so I cannot comment with certainty. But they were great personalities who gave humanity valuable teachings." The controversy began two days ago after a video of Etawah-based cleric Maulana Jarjis Ansari surfaced. In the video, he claimed that Lord Krishna was a Muslim and offered namaz five times a day. His remarks drew strong objections from Hindu organisations. The Hindu Mahasabha lodged an FIR at Hazratganj police station in Lucknow. Read ST Hasan's 2 major points- 1. Government should reconsider decision to demolish Jauhar University Responding to a question about the proposed demolition of Azam Khan's Jauhar University, ST Hasan said, "Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University is an educational institution where both Hindus and Muslims study. The government should reconsider its decision." He added, "An alternative solution should be found. Educational institutions are built with great difficulty. Azam Khan established this university. Individuals do not live forever, but institutions continue serving society. I appeal to the Chief Minister and the Governor to find a middle path in this matter." 2. 'One Nation, One Election' is not easy to implement Speaking on the proposed 'One Nation, One Election' system, ST Hasan said, "Governments in our country can fall before completing their term. If a government collapses midway, what will happen? Will elections wait until the scheduled date, or will President's Rule be imposed? That will create unnecessary competition and confusion." He added, "The party ruling at the Centre could try to bring down state governments and indirectly start governing them. Even now, governments are unable to conduct panchayat elections on time, yet they are talking about One Nation, One Election. Holding elections simultaneously for village panchayats, urban local bodies, district panchayats, state assemblies and Parliament is not practical. There are more challenges than benefits." What did Maulana Jarjis Ansari say? Maulana Jarjis Ansari made the remarks during a religious gathering in Deoghar, Jharkhand, on June 23. He said, "If our brothers do not mind, even Lord Krishna used to offer namaz five times a day. If you do not believe me, read the 10th verse of Chapter 6 of the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita." He then quoted the Sanskrit verse: Yogi yunjit satatam atmanam rahasi sthitah Ekaki yatachittatma nirashir aparigrahah. The Maulana claimed that in this verse Lord Krishna tells Arjuna that one should worship God with the entire body. He said, "'Yogi' does not mean the Yogi from Uttar Pradesh. 'Yogi yunjit satatam atmanam' means connect your whole body while worshipping. Worship should not be performed only by standing. The entire body should be involved. Today, if you look at Hindu worship, people simply raise their hands and say 'Om Namah Shivaya' and consider the worship complete." He further claimed, “If Hindus and Muslims read their own religious books, Yogi ji, who considers himself a great devotee of Lord Ram, would begin to love Islam after reading his own scriptures. Islam is not only the religion of Muslims; it belongs to them as well. The same faith was presented by Lord Ram and Lord Krishna. It is not exclusive to Muslims.” Cleric accused of misinterpreting Gita verse Maulana Jarjis Ansari has been accused of misinterpreting the Bhagavad Gita verse to support his claim. The verse makes no reference to namaz or Islam. The verse is Chapter 6, Verse 10 of the Bhagavad Gita. Its actual meaning is that a yogi should constantly focus his mind, body and soul on the Supreme Being. A person should meditate in solitude, control the mind and senses, and free themselves from desires and attachments.

stories.title: If you have a daughter, know about these 5 schemes:Support available from birth to education and marriage; here's how to apply
stories.summary: Five major schemes are running for daughters in Uttar Pradesh. Financial assistance is provided from birth to education and then marriage. The application process is very easy. However, many families are unable to take advantage due to lack of information. Let's understand these five schemes in detail. 1. Chief Minister Kanya Sumangala Scheme The objective of this scheme is to empower daughters by providing them financial assistance from birth to higher education. In 2024, the UP government increased the total assistance amount of this scheme from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000. Money is transferred to the daughter's bank account as follows: If you have twin daughters, you can still apply The beneficiary's family must be a permanent resident of UP. The total annual income of the family should be ₹3 lakh or less. A maximum of two daughters per family can avail the benefits of this scheme. If twin daughters are born in the second delivery, all three will receive benefits. If a family has legally adopted an orphan daughter, a maximum of two daughters, including their own daughters and the adopted daughter, will receive the benefits of this scheme. The scheme was launched in 2019 to eliminate female feticide, prevent child marriage, and improve the education level of daughters. 2. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana A Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account can be opened in the name of a daughter under 10 years of age. A family can open an account for maximum of two daughters. However, in special situations like having twins or triplets, the rules will accommodate. The account can only be opened by the daughter's parents or legal guardian. Investment Limit: A minimum of ₹250 and a maximum of ₹1.5 lakh can be deposited in a financial year. Interest Rate: Currently, the government is offering interest at an annual rate of 8.2 per cent on this scheme. Interest rates may also change every quarter. Tax Exemption: The amount deposited, the interest received, and the maturity amount are fully exempt under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act (in the Old Tax Regime). Maturity: This account matures upon completion of 21 years, but up to 50 per cent of the amount can be withdrawn for higher education once the daughter crosses 18 years of age. The account can also be closed before the maturity date under specific conditions, such as the death of the account holder. 3. Chief Minister Mass Marriage Scheme Under this scheme, assistance is provided for the marriage of daughters from economically weak families. Financial assistance is also provided for the remarriage of widowed and divorced women under the scheme. Under this scheme, the UP government spends a total of ₹1 lakh on the marriage of each couple. To avail the benefits of the scheme, the girl's age must be at least 18 years and the boy's age must be at least 21 years. Families from all categories including Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), Other Backward Class (OBC), General, and Minorities can apply. The family's annual income should be ₹3 lakh or less. The applicant must be a native resident of UP. 4. Uttar Pradesh Rani Lakshmibai Mahila Evam Bal Samman Kosh (Women and Child Honour Fund) Under this scheme, daughters and women who are victims of severe violence receive immediate treatment and financial assistance. Victim girls are provided assistance ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹10 lakh, depending on the severity of the crime. Treatment is completely free in government or empanelled hospitals. If needed, the government also helps with their accommodation, education, treatment, and restarting a normal life. If the victim has young children, there is also a provision for financial assistance and other necessary help for their education and upbringing. 5. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Yojana (Save Girl Child, Educate Girl Child Scheme) Under this scheme, free bags, uniforms, and stationery are provided to girls. Campaigns are run to prevent school dropouts, and efforts are made to improve the gender ratio of boys and girls. Girls are also provided with free residential education through Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas. Answers to 2 important questions related to schemes Question: Can one avail benefits of multiple government schemes simultaneously? Answer: Yes, absolutely. If your daughter is eligible, she can simultaneously avail benefits of Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana for education, Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana for future funds, and Mass Marriage Scheme when she grows up. stories.title: Yogi vows action in Lalita Gautam murder case:Meets bereaved family, announces ₹5 lakh relief and house; CM visits sister in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath met with the victim's family of the Lalita Gautam murder case on Saturday in Ghaziabad. Yogi told the student's parents that the culprits will not be spared and the strictest punishment will be sought for. The CM announced financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to the family and aid for one home each to the victim's father and uncle. Earlier, former IPS officer and Meerut in-charge minister Asim Arun reached the PWD Guest House in Ghaziabad at 9:30 am to meet Lalita Gautam's family. Then Asim arranged the family's meeting with the CM. CM Yogi expressed grief over the incident. He obtained information about the action taken so far from police officers. Earlier, Yogi reached the house of his sister Pushpa Chaudhary in Muradnagar, Ghaziabad at 9 pm on Friday. As soon as Yogi arrived at MGI Gharaunda Society located in Rajnagar Extension, people came out of their flats. They started chanting 'Jai Shri Ram'. Yogi stayed at his sister's house for about 45 minutes. Later he took photos with the children in the area. What Yogi said to the victim's family Ikra had arranged the victim's family's meeting with Akhilesh Yadav SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had met with the victim's family six days ago. Akhilesh spoke with Lalita's family for 1 hour and 15 minutes in a closed room at his government residence in Delhi. He had handed them a cheque of ₹2 lakh. According to sources, on the night of July 10 (Friday), Akhilesh called the family and invited them to meet him in Delhi. Kairana MP Iqra Hasan reached Delhi with the victim's parents and brother. Akhilesh told Lalita's father that their daughter will get justice. When the government is formed, one member of the family will be given a job. He also took a dig at Meerut's SSP Avinash Pandey. He said the police, from whom justice is expected, is slapping injustice and arrogance on the cheeks of the public. MP Chandrashekhar met the family Earlier, on July 10, MP Chandrashekhar Azad had met Lalita's family members in Meerut. The MP gave a seven-day ultimatum to the administration saying, “If justice is not delivered, we will protest in Lucknow and will also raise the matter in Lok Sabha.” Details of the Lalita Gautam murder case CM had halted in Ghaziabad for night rest

stories.title: 'Crocodile swallowed my nephew, I could only watch':Uncle recounts horror; sisters mourn clutching bloodstained sheet
stories.summary: A 12-year-old boy was killed in a crocodile attack in Bahraich district after the reptile dragged him into the Ghaghara River while he was washing his hands and feet with his uncle. Despite desperate attempts by family members and villagers to save him, the crocodile disappeared into the river with the child. His body was recovered nearly three hours later. 'I watched helplessly as the crocodile dragged him away' The victim's uncle, Uday Raj Singh, who witnessed the attack, said he was standing barely four metres away when the crocodile seized the boy. The crocodile had clamped its jaws around my nephew. My brother immediately jumped into the river and tried to pull him back, but the crocodile kept dragging him deeper into the water. We were helpless as it disappeared with him. According to eyewitnesses, villagers pelted the crocodile with stones and bricks in an attempt to make it release the child, but it remained underwater for nearly three hours. Body recovered after three hours Villagers said the crocodile resurfaced at around 7:30 p.m., still holding the boy in its jaws and repeatedly thrashing the body. By then, teams from the police, Forest Department, and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) had reached the spot. Local resident Inspector Singh, carrying a fishing net, helped recover the child's body from the river. Sisters mourn beside blood-stained shroud When reporters visited Tikuri village on Friday, the boy had already been cremated. The blood-stained sheet in which his body had been wrapped after being brought out of the river lay in the house. His sisters were inconsolable—one gently caressed the stained cloth while another cried uncontrollably, resting her head on the shroud. Parents had already passed away The deceased, Sunil, had lost both his parents several years ago. His father died five years ago and his mother seven years ago due to illness. He was the second of four siblings: Following his parents' deaths, Sunil had been living with his uncle, Vijay Raj Singh. While his siblings continue to study at the village primary school, Sunil had dropped out of school. Attack occurred after returning from the fields According to villagers, Sunil had accompanied his uncle to transplant paddy in the fields on Thursday afternoon. After working for several hours, they stopped at the Ghaghara River to wash themselves before heading home. It was then that the crocodile suddenly emerged from the water and attacked the boy. His uncle raised an alarm, and nearby farmers rushed to help. Despite repeated attempts, the villagers could not free the child from the crocodile's grip. Search continued into the night Villagers launched a search operation using long bamboo poles and searched nearly 500 metres downstream, as the river was flowing swiftly. Even after darkness fell, the search continued under torchlight. The body, badly mutilated in the attack, was eventually recovered and police were informed. On Friday morning, police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Authorities are continuing to monitor the area following the fatal crocodile attack.

stories.title: Heavy rain floods Gorakhpur, swells Ganga in Varanasi:SP office waterlogged in Pratapgarh; Ganga Aarti venue shifted
stories.summary: The southwest monsoon has regained strength across Uttar Pradesh, bringing heavy rainfall to several parts of the state and causing widespread waterlogging, rising river levels, and flood concerns. By 7 a.m. on Saturday, rain had been reported in Gorakhpur, Bareilly, Agra, and several other cities. Gorakhpur witnessed intense rainfall that submerged roads, leaving cars partially underwater and forcing commuters to push motorcycles and scooters through knee-deep water. Cloudy conditions prevailed in more than 30 cities, including Lucknow and Kanpur, since morning. Rain disrupts normal life in several cities On Friday, rainfall was recorded in nearly 20 cities, including Varanasi, Prayagraj, and Pratapgarh. In Pratapgarh, rainwater entered the office of the Superintendent of Police (SP), causing waterlogging inside the premises. In Varanasi, the rising water level of the Ganga River forced authorities to shift the venue of the Ganga Aarti at Lalita Ghat. The daily ritual will now be conducted at a higher and safer location on the steps until water levels recede. In Prayagraj, a car became trapped after a roadside drain collapsed due to the rain. Statewide rain alert issued The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for the entire state. Thunderstorms accompanied by rain and lightning are likely in 31 cities during the day. According to the IMD, the monsoon has become active once again over Uttar Pradesh, and rainfall is expected to continue over the coming days. The weather department has advised residents to remain alert and avoid unnecessary travel during periods of heavy rain. Rivers in spate after heavy rain in hills Heavy rainfall in the Himalayan region has also caused water levels in major rivers flowing through Uttar Pradesh to rise. At the Sangam in Prayagraj, the water levels of both the Ganga and Yamuna are increasing, prompting authorities to make public announcements asking people to stay away from the riverbanks. The Saryu River in Ballia and Barabanki has also risen close to the danger mark, putting 87 villages under the threat of flooding. Monsoon to intensify over the next week Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Meteorologist at the IMD's Lucknow Centre, said the revival of the monsoon is being driven by a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal. He said the system has already triggered rainfall across eastern Uttar Pradesh and is expected to cover western parts of the state as well. According to the meteorologist, the strengthening weather system is likely to keep the monsoon active, with heavy rainfall expected across Uttar Pradesh over the next week.

stories.title: Meerut woman gets husband bitten by snake:Rushed his body to hospital; allegedly drugged him with sleeping pills in milk, couple had love marriage
stories.summary: Police have claimed to have solved the mysterious death of a private school operator in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut, alleging that his wife conspired with her lover and two snake charmers to murder him by using a venomous snake. According to investigators, the accused first mixed an overdose of sleeping pills into the victim's milk before releasing a venomous snake into his blanket, causing the fatal snakebite while he was unconscious. Police have arrested the victim's wife, her alleged lover, and two snake charmers in connection with the case. Body taken to hospital after death The victim's body was found on a bed in a rented house at around 6 a.m. on Friday. His wife and other family members rushed him to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Soon after the incident, the victim's relatives accused the wife of orchestrating the murder through a snakebite. Police detained her for questioning and examined her call records. Frequent conversations with the school's van driver raised suspicion, following which the driver allegedly confessed to the crime. See 2 pictures- Wife's initial version to police During preliminary questioning, the wife told police that she had shifted to another room with their six-year-old son at around 2 a.m. to sleep. She claimed that when she returned to the bedroom in the morning, her husband was lying under a blanket. After receiving no response despite repeatedly calling him, she removed the blanket and saw a snake, after which she screamed. Investigators later found snakebite marks on the victim's right leg. Based on the family's complaint, police sent the body for a post-mortem examination. The incident took place in the Hastinapur police station area of Meerut. Victim ran a private school The deceased, Atul Kumar (32), was a resident of Bhandora village in Bahsuma. He had been living in a rented house in Hastinapur with his wife Damini (30) and their six-year-old son. The couple had been running Krishna Kids Play School for the past four years. The school, located about a kilometre from their residence, caters to students from nursery to Class 5 and has around 150 students. Couple had a love marriage Family members said Atul and Damini had a love marriage seven years ago. Before opening the school, Atul worked at a private computer company. Atul was the youngest of three brothers. His father, Ajab Singh (72), is a farmer, while his mother, Santosh Devi (69), is a homemaker. His elder brother is a retired Army personnel, and another brother died by suicide four years ago. According to the family, they had already suspected Damini and informed the police after receiving news of Atul's death. Police claim driver confessed CO Mawana Pankaj Lavania said the local police and forensic team collected evidence from the crime scene immediately after receiving information about the death. "Based on call detail records, the school's van driver, Tushar, was taken into custody. During questioning, he allegedly confessed to the murder conspiracy," the officer said. Police have arrested Tushar, Damini, and two snake charmers identified as Sonu and Uday. Further investigation into the case is underway.

stories.title: Ram Mandir theft accused Tinnu gets VIP treatment in jail:TV, sofa, mosquito repellent provided; claimed to have better facilities than an MLA
stories.summary: "What kind of treatment would even an MLA get that Tinnu Yadav is getting in jail? There is a TV in his barrack, sofas to sit on, clean bedding, and even a mosquito repellent machine." This claim has been made by a neighbour of Ramshankar alias Tinnu Yadav, one of the main accused in the Ram Mandir offerings theft case, after meeting him at Faizabad Jail. According to the neighbour, visitors are lining up to meet Tinnu, and despite spending 22 days in jail, "his influence is clearly visible." Residents of the locality also claim that after allegations surfaced that Tinnu stole gold and silver offerings from the Ram Mandir, women in his family have stopped wearing jewellery. The family reportedly remained confined to their house for several days before gradually resuming their daily routine. Neighbours reluctant to reveal Tinnu's address Tinnu Yadav lives in Swarn Dwar locality, about 3 km from the Ram Mandir. His three brothers also have houses in the same neighbourhood. His family includes his wife, Poonam, and son Ravi, a contractual employee in the Public Works Department (PWD), who got married about six to seven months ago. One of Tinnu's brothers, Dinesh, has died. Dinesh's sons, Manish and Sunny, were allegedly given jobs at the Ram Mandir through Tinnu. Manish has also been arrested in the donation theft case. When journalists visited the locality, most residents refused to identify Tinnu's house or speak on record. Hidden-camera conversations, however, suggested that the neighbourhood has changed significantly since the arrests. Residents say jewellery has disappeared from the house A 60-year-old resident said relatives frequently visit Tinnu's house in the evenings and at night but do not stay long. Another resident claimed Tinnu always wore a thick gold chain and that other family members also wore gold and silver jewellery. "Since the theft case surfaced, even the women in the family have stopped wearing jewellery. We feel all the valuables have been removed from the house." Residents also claimed that Tinnu's wife Poonam is no longer seen wearing jewellery and that the Bullet motorcycle he frequently rode has also disappeared, possibly moved to a relative's house. 'High-profile arrangements inside jail' The reporters also met Birendra Tiwari, a former municipal councillor candidate, who claimed to have recently met Tinnu in jail. "Earlier, at least 1,000 policemen worked under Tinnu's supervision, and even today his influence hasn't diminished. He is in jail, but his stature remains the same." Tiwari further claimed: He himself told us there are four sofa chairs in his barrack. There is a mosquito repellent machine and a TV. There is a constant queue of visitors waiting to meet him. Other accused have not received such facilities, but he has been given VIP treatment. When asked about allegations linking Tinnu to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Tiwari dismissed them. “This is complete nonsense. They have been associated with the BJP for nearly 30 years and have campaigned for the party. They have no connection whatsoever with Akhilesh Yadav or the Samajwadi Party. If you speak to Tinnu, you'll hear him criticise the Samajwadi Party himself.” DIG responds to VIP treatment claims Responding to the allegations, Ayodhya Range DIG Shailendra Kumar Maitreya said, The special barrack where Tinnu Yadav has been lodged is equipped with CCTV cameras. I have instructed the jail superintendent to closely monitor him. Only the selected individuals whose names were provided by Tinnu are allowed to meet him. 'He could get anyone a job in Ram Mandir' A local shopkeeper alleged that Tinnu became extremely influential after the Ram Mandir was built. "If he wanted someone to get a job at the Ram Mandir, it would happen. I requested him to help my brother, but he didn't. He got jobs for both his nephews and one of his brothers. Many of his close associates also got jobs." The shopkeeper added that despite his influence, Tinnu or his immediate family rarely participated in neighbourhood matters, unlike his brothers. Fond of expensive motorcycles and authority Another shopkeeper described Tinnu as someone who loved motorcycles. He first bought a black HF Deluxe, then a red bike, and later a Bullet. While riding, he always carried a walkie-talkie clipped to his shirt pocket at full volume, issuing instructions. If someone parked a vehicle in front of him, he would abuse them. People knew his influence, so nobody objected. Temple vendors say footfall has dropped A flower seller near the historic Nageshwar Nath Temple, about 200 metres from Tinnu's house, claimed the theft has damaged Ayodhya's image. "Ever since Tinnu and seven others were accused of theft, Ayodhya has been defamed. The number of visitors has fallen by nearly 75%. If fewer people are visiting the Ram Mandir, even fewer are coming to Nageshwar Temple." The vendor demanded financial recovery from the accused and strict action. Recovery should be made from them. People need to see that strict action is being taken so that such incidents are not repeated. Only then will public confidence return. Some locals defend Tinnu Not everyone in the area believes the allegations. Aditya Yadav, a shopkeeper originally from Bahraich, said: “I feel Tinnu is being targeted because he is a Yadav. Since the days of the Ram temple movement, he has worked hard and operated two or three auto-rickshaws. That's how he earned his money. People say he has a sofa in jail, but perhaps others also have chairs. After all, they too are accused.” Investigators say Tinnu held the keys to donation lockers The investigation has revealed that among the eight arrested accused, Tinnu Yadav held the most influential position. Police say he was present whenever donation boxes were opened in the counting room and also accompanied the cash during its transfer to the bank after counting. His nephew Manish was allegedly caught on CCTV stealing from the donation collections. During searches, police recovered ₹1 lakh in cash from Tinnu and ₹2 lakh from Manish. Before his arrest, Tinnu had released a video claiming innocence. He said all his properties were acquired through earnings from operating tempo vehicles and by investing money received after selling ancestral land in 2008. On Friday evening, police obtained 38-hour custody remand of both Tinnu and Manish and are expected to conduct fresh rounds of interrogation.

stories.title: IAS once labelled 'unworthy' by Azam to decide university's fate:₹100 crore payment due; three ways to escape from bulldozer action
stories.summary: Time has come full circle for Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan. The IAS officer whom Khan had publicly mocked in 2019 as a "tankhwaiya" (salaried employee) and said he wanted to make him clean his shoes is now in a position to decide the future of Rampur's Jauhar University. Commissioner heads authority overseeing demolition order Anjaneya Singh, Commissioner of the Moradabad Division, serves as the Chairman of the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) and is also the Appellate Authority. On July 15, the RDA's Vice Chairman and Rampur District Magistrate, Ajay Kumar Dwivedi, issued an order directing the demolition of the university over alleged building plan violations. Experts estimate compliance could cost over ₹100 crore Architects familiar with the case say Azam Khan may have to spend more than Rs 100 crore if he wants to save the university from demolition. They say he currently has three legal options. Three options before Azam Khan The first option is to get building plans for all 38 structures regularised through the RDA's compounding process. However, this would require payment of substantial charges, including development fees, labour cess, compounding charges and impact fees. The second option is to challenge the demolition order before the High Court. However, even if he obtains legal relief, approval of the building plans will ultimately have to be secured from the RDA. The third option is to approach Moradabad Commissioner Anjaneya Singh in his capacity as the Appellate Authority and seek a stay on the RDA's demolition order. Read how Azam Khan failed to get the map approved Following the demolition notice issued for 38 buildings at Jauhar University, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to architects and officials associated with the case. The inquiry revealed that Singankhedi village, where the university is located, was brought under the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) in March 2026. Until then, the village fell under the jurisdiction of the district panchayat. Under the district panchayat, development charges ranged from ₹100 to ₹300 per square metre. Experts said that if Azam Khan had obtained building approvals before the area was brought under the RDA, the entire university campus could have been regularised for around ₹5–6 crore. However, the approvals were never secured before the jurisdiction changed. Architects say - Now will have to go to RDA only to get maps approved Senior architects associated with the case say that regardless of which court Azam Khan approaches, approval of the university's building plans will ultimately have to come from the Rampur Development Authority (RDA). They added that if he wants the demolition order stayed, he can also file an appeal before the RDA Chairman, Moradabad Commissioner Anjaneya Singh. Experts say the option to regularise the university buildings is still available. To begin the process, Azam Khan must first submit an application through the Uttar Pradesh government's Nivesh Mitra portal and obtain nine mandatory online No Objection Certificates (NOCs) before seeking approval of the building plans. Once the required NOCs are obtained, the university will have to submit a building plan application to the Rampur Development Authority through a registered architect. The approval process will require payment of several statutory charges before the plans can be regularised. Development charges, labour cess and compounding fee applicable According to experts, the RDA levies a development charge of ₹1,510 per square metre. However, the final amount depends on factors such as the covered area and the overall size of the project, and can only be assessed after examining the building plans. In addition, a labour cess of 1% of the total project cost will have to be paid. If Jauhar University's project cost is assessed at ₹1,000 crore, the labour cess alone would come to around ₹10 crore. The university would also have to pay a compounding fee, which is imposed for constructing buildings without obtaining prior approval of the building plans. Development fees and fines could reach up to ₹100 crores Officials of the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) estimate that Azam Khan may have to pay nearly ₹100 crore in fees and penalties if he seeks to regularise Jauhar University's buildings. The amount would include development charges, compounding fees, impact fees and other statutory payments. Officials, however, said the exact liability can only be determined after examining the university's complete layout plan, covered area and other project details. They also pointed out that, as a minority educational institution, Jauhar University may be eligible for certain exemptions provided under government rules, which could reduce the overall financial burden. Land-use issue may become another hurdle Senior architects say the land-use classification of the university campus will be a crucial factor. If the land is not designated for educational purposes, it will first have to be converted before the building plans can be approved. Such a change would require payment of a substantial impact fee to the RDA. Even then, the proposal would have to be cleared by the RDA Board and forwarded to the state government for approval. Experts believe that, given the current political circumstances, the chances of such a proposal being approved and sent to the government are slim. If university buildings fall in green belt, troubles will increase Under Uttar Pradesh's planning laws, development authorities do not have the power to change the land use of areas designated as Green Belt in the Master Plan. Since Green Belt zones are meant to preserve environmental balance, any change requires approval from the state government and compliance with statutory procedures. Experts say that if any construction is found within a Green Belt area, its land use cannot be regularised merely by paying impact fees, making such violations significantly harder to resolve. University now falls under RDA jurisdiction Another challenge for Azam Khan stems from the expansion of the Rampur Development Authority's jurisdiction. The RDA was constituted under the Uttar Pradesh Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973, and initially functioned under the Rampur Master Plan 2005, which governed the city's residential, commercial and industrial development. Although that Master Plan expired in 2005, the authority's boundaries were later expanded as the city grew. Following this expansion, Mohammad Ali Jauhar University came within the jurisdiction of the RDA. New Master Plan could decide university's future At its meeting in March 2026, the RDA included 39 new revenue villages under the proposed Rampur Master Plan 2031, including Singankheda, where Mohammad Ali Jauhar University is located. Under the rules, the RDA Board will prepare the draft Master Plan 2031 and determine the land-use classification of these newly added areas before forwarding it to the state government for approval. The Board is headed by Moradabad Commissioner Anjaneya Singh, with the Rampur District Magistrate serving as Vice-Chairman. Experts believe the land-use classification under the new Master Plan could emerge as one of the biggest legal hurdles for Azam Khan in the battle to save Jauhar University. What is the ‘Tankhayya’ controversy, know... The matter is from 2019. The Lok Sabha election campaign was echoing in every street. At that time, SP and Bahujan Samaj Party were contesting elections in alliance. The Rampur Lok Sabha seat had come to SP's share. Azam Khan himself was a candidate. During the election campaign, a video of Azam surfaced, in which he was saying- Everyone stand firm, don't be afraid of the Collector-Follector, they are salaried employees, we are not afraid of them. I have seen many photos of Mayawati. How big officers used to take out handkerchiefs and keep cleaning shoes. We have an alliance with them, if Allah wills, I will make them clean their shoes… ... At that time, the DM of Rampur was Aanjaneya Kumar Singh, who is now the Commissioner of Moradabad. On his instructions, the then Tanda SDM Ghanshyam Tripathi had filed an FIR against Azam Khan for hate speech at Bhot police station. After 6 years, on May 16, 2026, the court sentenced Azam Khan to 2 years imprisonment.

stories.title: Supreme Court protest costs Lucknow University students:Suspended over alleged abuse of CJI; papers thrown in courtroom
stories.summary: Lucknow University has suspended two LLB students with immediate effect on charges of allegedly obstructing proceedings in the Supreme Court. A video of both students had surfaced. Later, it also went viral on social media. In the video, they were seen allegedly creating a ruckus inside the Supreme Court, throwing papers at the judge, and using abusive language against the Chief Justice of India (CJI). The university administration has taken action after an FIR was registered in the case. Based on the recommendations of the committee constituted by the Additional Proctor of LU's Second Campus, both students have been suspended until the investigation is complete. Hostel Room Also Canceled, Entry to Campus Prohibited According to the university notice, the suspended students include Surendra Singh and Chandra Bhan, fifth-semester students of the three-year LLB course. Both have been barred from entering the premises of Lucknow University during the investigation period. Additionally, the allocation of hostel rooms assigned to both students has also been cancelled. They have also been deprived of student-related facilities. The students have been instructed to submit their written explanation within three working days. LU spokesperson Mukul Srivastava stated that further disciplinary action would be taken against the students based on the investigation report. Police had arrested According to the police, both students were arrested on charges of allegedly creating a ruckus during a hearing in the Supreme Court, using abusive language against the CJI, throwing papers at the judge, and assaulting a security guard. An FIR has been registered in the case on charges related to conduct prejudicial to the dignity of a constitutional institution like the Supreme Court. The university administration has stated that further action will be taken based on the report after the investigation is complete.
